subject: Physiology
topic: Cardiac Ventricular Action Potential Phase 3 Repolarization
shortestValidSolution: Identify KCNQ1 -> encodes IKs potassium channel -> responsible for phase 3 repolarization -> delayed repolarization causes long QT.
necessaryInference: Connect KCNQ1 mutation to specific action potential phase (phase 3) rather than general arrhythmia or sodium influx.
strongestDistractor: Phase 2 plateau duration prolongation, which is influenced by IKs but primarily governed by Cav1.2 L-type calcium channels.
distractorExclusion: Cav1.2 governs phase 2; KCNQ1 specifically mediates outward phase 3 rapid/slow delayed repolarization.

references.label: Circulation 2022 Congenital Long-QT Syndrome: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen / Romano-Ward Mechanisms

subject: Physiology
topic: Renal Tubular Transport & Loop of Henle NKCC2 Transporter Defects
shortestValidSolution: Hypercalciuria + nephrocalcinosis + hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis + low BP = thick ascending limb NKCC2 defect (Bartter syndrome).
necessaryInference: Use hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis to distinguish thick ascending limb (Bartter) from distal convoluted tubule (Gitelman, which has hypocalciuria).
strongestDistractor: Distal convoluted tubule NCCT defect (Gitelman syndrome), which causes identical alkalosis and hypokalemia but low urinary calcium.
distractorExclusion: High urinary calcium and nephrocalcinosis definitively exclude Gitelman syndrome.

references.label: Kidney International 2021 Consensus statement on the diagnosis and management of Bartter syndrome

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Sulfur Amino Acid Metabolism & Cystathionine Beta-Synthase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Marfanoid habitus + inferonasal lens dislocation + pediatric stroke + elevated methionine = cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency.
necessaryInference: Distinguish CBS deficiency from Marfan syndrome (normal homocysteine) and methionine synthase deficiency (low methionine).
strongestDistractor: Fibrillin-1 mutation (Marfan syndrome), which shares arachnodactyly and pectus excavatum.
distractorExclusion: Elevated homocysteine, thromboembolic stroke, and inferonasal (downward) lens dislocation exclude Marfan syndrome.

references.label: GeneReviews 2020 Cystathionine Beta-Synthase Deficiency / Homocystinuria

subject: Microbiology
topic: Bacterial Exotoxin ADP-Ribosylation of Elongation Factor-2
shortestValidSolution: Leathery pharyngeal pseudomembrane + bull neck + AV block = diphtheria toxin -> ADP-ribosylates EF-2.
necessaryInference: Identify Corynebacterium diphtheriae from classic presentation and recall its specific enzymatic target (EF-2 ADP-ribosylation).
strongestDistractor: Cleavage of 28S rRNA (Shiga toxin), which also halts protein synthesis but via N-glycosidase activity on rRNA rather than ADP-ribosylation of EF-2.
distractorExclusion: Diphtheria toxin specifically transfers ADP-ribose to EF-2; it does not cleave 28S rRNA.

references.label: CDC Diphtheria Clinical Features and Pathology Guide 2022

subject: Immunology
topic: Renal Allograft Hyperacute Rejection & Preformed Antibody Complement Activation
shortestValidSolution: Cyanosis and anuria 25 minutes after unclamping + microvascular fibrin thrombi = hyperacute rejection via preformed anti-donor antibodies.
necessaryInference: Connect rapid intraoperative failure (minutes) to preformed antibodies rather than cell-mediated acute rejection (weeks).
strongestDistractor: Host CD8+ T lymphocyte mediated rejection (acute cellular rejection), which is the most common cause of allograft dysfunction weeks to months later.
distractorExclusion: Cellular tubulitis takes days to weeks to generate; 25-minute failure is exclusively antibody/complement-mediated.

references.label: New England Journal of Medicine 2021 Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Kidney Transplantation

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Organophosphate Toxicity & Acetylcholinesterase Regeneration
shortestValidSolution: Organophosphate poisoning: atropine fixes muscarinic symptoms (bronchospasm/bradycardia); pralidoxime regenerates AChE to reverse nicotinic weakness.
necessaryInference: Recognize that persistent skeletal muscle weakness reflects nicotinic receptor overstimulation unresponsive to atropine.
strongestDistractor: Physostigmine, which is used for anticholinergic toxicity (the opposite condition) and would worsen organophosphate toxicity.
distractorExclusion: Physostigmine is an AChE inhibitor; giving more AChE inhibition to an organophosphate poisoning is lethal.

references.label: Toxicology Reviews 2021 Organophosphate Toxicity: Mechanisms, Atropine, and Oximes

subject: Pathology
topic: Carbon Tetrachloride Hepatotoxicity & Lipid Peroxidation
shortestValidSolution: Carbon tetrachloride -> CYP2E1 creates CCl3• radical -> lipid peroxidation disrupts RER -> decreased ApoB-100 synthesis -> trapped triglycerides (fatty liver).
necessaryInference: Connect solvent exposure to free radical disruption of protein synthesis (ApoB-100) and VLDL export block.
strongestDistractor: NADH/NAD+ ratio shift from alcohol dehydrogenase, which is the mechanism of alcoholic fatty liver.
distractorExclusion: Alcoholic fatty liver involves ethanol metabolism; CCl4 causes direct free radical membrane peroxidative damage.

references.label: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease 10th ed. Mechanisms of Free Radical Injury and Steatosis

subject: Genetics
topic: Genomic Imprinting & Prader-Willi vs Angelman Syndrome Mechanisms
shortestValidSolution: Hyperphagia + infantile hypotonia + maternal isodisomy = maternal meiosis II non-disjunction with trisomy rescue.
necessaryInference: Connect isodisomy (identical copies) specifically to meiosis II non-disjunction, distinguishing from heterodisomy (meiosis I).
strongestDistractor: Maternal meiosis I non-disjunction, which causes maternal heterodisomy rather than isodisomy.
distractorExclusion: Meiosis I failure separates homologues and produces heterodisomy; isodisomy requires sister chromatid failure in meiosis II.

references.label: GeneReviews 2021 Prader-Willi Syndrome: Clinical Genetics and UPD Mechanisms

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Erythrocyte Glycolytic Enzymopathy & Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Chronic hemolytic anemia + splenomegaly + elevated 2,3-BPG + burr cells = pyruvate kinase deficiency (glycolytic ATP generation failure).
necessaryInference: Use the 3-fold elevation in 2,3-BPG to point directly to a block below 1,3-BPG in glycolysis (pyruvate kinase).
strongestDistractor: G6PD deficiency, which also causes red cell enzymopathy but is episodic, oxidative, and characterized by Heinz bodies and normal 2,3-BPG.
distractorExclusion: High 2,3-BPG and lack of oxidative triggers rule out G6PD deficiency.

references.label: Blood 2020 Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency: Clinical Manifestations and Pathophysiology

subject: Anatomy
topic: Spinal Cord Hemisection (Brown-Séquard Syndrome) Tract Organization
shortestValidSolution: Right hemisection: ipsilateral corticospinal (motor) + ipsilateral dorsal columns (vibration) + contralateral spinothalamic (pain/temp).
necessaryInference: Apply tract decussation levels: corticospinal/dorsal columns cross in medulla (ipsilateral deficit); spinothalamic crosses in cord (contralateral deficit).
strongestDistractor: Contralateral spastic paresis, a common error when learners confuse cord lesions with cerebral/brainstem lesions.
distractorExclusion: Corticospinal tract decussates in the medulla; spinal cord lesion causes ipsilateral weakness.

references.label: StatPearls 2023 Brown-Sequard Syndrome Neuroanatomy and Clinical Presentation

subject: Physiology
topic: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia & 11-Beta-Hydroxylase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Ambiguous female genitalia (androgen excess) + hypertension + elevated 11-DOC = 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency.
necessaryInference: Use the presence of hypertension to distinguish 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency from 21-hydroxylase deficiency.
strongestDistractor: 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which is much more common and shares female virilization.
distractorExclusion: 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypotension and hyperkalemia; elevated blood pressure and hypokalemia require 11-DOC excess.

references.label: Endocrine Reviews 2021 Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia: Clinical Diagnosis and Enzymatic Profiling

subject: Physiology
topic: Canalicular Bilirubin Excretion & MRP2 Transporter Mutations
shortestValidSolution: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia + dark granular lysosomal liver pigment = Dubin-Johnson syndrome -> defective canalicular MRP2 transporter.
necessaryInference: Use the presence of dark lysosomal liver pigment to differentiate Dubin-Johnson (MRP2 defect) from Rotor syndrome (OATP defect, no pigment).
strongestDistractor: Rotor syndrome (OATP1B1/OATP1B3 defect), which also causes benign conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
distractorExclusion: Rotor syndrome has completely normal liver color and lacks the dark brown/black lysosomal pigment seen in Dubin-Johnson.

references.label: Hepatology Communications 2021 Inherited Disorders of Bilirubin Clearance and Transport

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Lipopeptide Antibiotics & Daptomycin Calcium-Dependent Membrane Disruption
shortestValidSolution: MRSA therapy + high creatine kinase (myopathy) = daptomycin -> calcium-dependent bacterial membrane pore formation and potassium efflux.
necessaryInference: Identify daptomycin from MRSA bacteremia + elevated CK, then identify its calcium-dependent membrane disruption mechanism.
strongestDistractor: Binding to D-Ala-D-Ala (vancomycin), the standard MRSA first-line agent, which causes red man syndrome and nephrotoxicity rather than myopathy.
distractorExclusion: Vancomycin does not cause direct muscle injury or high CK; myopathy is the signature toxicity of daptomycin.

references.label: Clinical Infectious Diseases 2020 Daptomycin-Induced Myopathy and Mechanism of Action

subject: Immunology
topic: Immunodeficiency with Hyper-IgM & CD40 Ligand (CD154) Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Elevated IgM + absent IgG/IgA + Pneumocystis/Cryptosporidium + normal B-cell count = CD40 ligand (CD154) deficiency.
necessaryInference: Identify CD40L defect from the pairing of class-switch failure (high IgM, low IgG/A) with opportunistic infections (macrophage impairment).
strongestDistractor: Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) deficiency, which also causes low IgG and IgA, but has absent B cells and profoundly low IgM.
distractorExclusion: BTK deficiency causes pan-hypogammaglobulinemia (including low IgM) and absent CD19+ B cells; hyper-IgM has elevated IgM and normal B-cell numbers.

references.label: Journal of Clinical Immunology 2020 Hyper IgM Syndromes: Clinical, Immunological, and Genetic Characteristics

subject: Pathology
topic: Neurocutaneous Syndromes & Sturge-Weber GNAQ Somatic Mosaicism
shortestValidSolution: Port-wine stain in V1 distribution + seizures + "tram-track" cortical calcifications = Sturge-Weber syndrome -> somatic mosaic GNAQ mutation.
necessaryInference: Connect classic clinical triad to somatic mosaicism in GNAQ, ruling out germline tumor suppressor syndromes.
strongestDistractor: Autosomal dominant TSC1/TSC2 mutations (Tuberous sclerosis), which also causes childhood seizures and brain calcifications.
distractorExclusion: Tuberous sclerosis features ash-leaf spots and subependymal nodules, not port-wine stains or cortical tram-track calcifications.

references.label: Lancet Neurology 2021 Sturge-Weber Syndrome: Biology, Genetics, and Management

subject: Physiology
topic: Alveolar Gas Equation & Hypoxemia with Normal A-a Gradient
shortestValidSolution: PAO2 = 0.21*(447-47) - 28/0.8 = 49 mmHg. A-a gradient = 49 - 46 = 3 mmHg (normal). Low altitude PiO2.
necessaryInference: Execute the alveolar gas equation calculation at reduced barometric pressure to derive an A-a gradient of 3 mmHg.
strongestDistractor: Elevated A-a gradient from high-altitude pulmonary edema, which occurs after days, not 1 hour, and widens the gradient.
distractorExclusion: Normal A-a gradient of 3 mmHg excludes intrinsic pulmonary gas-exchange defects like HAPE or diffusion block.

references.label: West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials 11th ed. Chapter 5: Oxygen Transport from Air to Tissue

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Purine Salvage Pathway & HGPRT Deficiency PRPP Dynamics
shortestValidSolution: HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan) -> PRPP is not consumed -> elevated PRPP activates PRPP amidotransferase -> massive de novo purine synthesis.
necessaryInference: Connect salvage enzyme failure to accumulation of its substrate (PRPP) and feedforward activation of de novo synthesis.
strongestDistractor: Depletion of PRPP, an intuitive error if candidates assume a synthetic failure rather than substrate accumulation.
distractorExclusion: PRPP is the substrate consumed by HGPRT; failure of the enzyme causes PRPP accumulation, not depletion.

references.label: GeneReviews 2020 Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome and Purine Metabolism

subject: Microbiology
topic: Influenza Segmented Genome Reassortment (Antigenic Shift)
shortestValidSolution: Avian + human + swine gene combination producing pandemic = segmented genome genetic reassortment (antigenic shift).
necessaryInference: Connect multilineage gene segments to segmented genomic reassortment (antigenic shift) rather than point mutations (antigenic drift).
strongestDistractor: High-frequency point mutations from error-prone RNA polymerase, which is the mechanism of antigenic drift, not shift.
distractorExclusion: Point mutations alter individual amino acids (drift); whole-gene segment swapping across species requires a segmented genome (shift).

references.label: Nature Reviews Microbiology 2021 The Mechanism of Influenza Antigenic Shift and Pandemic Emergence

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Antifolate Pharmacodynamics & Leucovorin (Folinic Acid) Rescue Mechanism
shortestValidSolution: Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses DHFR -> directly replenishes tetrahydrofolate pool downstream of the methotrexate block.
necessaryInference: Recognize that leucovorin acts downstream of DHFR rather than displacing the drug or accelerating clearance.
strongestDistractor: Competitive displacement of methotrexate from DHFR, a common misconception of how rescue therapy functions.
distractorExclusion: Leucovorin does not remove methotrexate from DHFR; it provides the downstream metabolite that DHFR failed to make.

references.label: Journal of Clinical Oncology 2021 Leucovorin Rescue in High-Dose Methotrexate Protocols

subject: Pathology
topic: Membranous Nephropathy & Phospholipase A2 Receptor Autoantibodies
shortestValidSolution: Nephrotic syndrome + anti-PLA2R antibodies = membranous nephropathy -> subepithelial immune deposits with "spike-and-dome" pattern.
necessaryInference: Identify membranous nephropathy from anti-PLA2R serology and map to subepithelial spike-and-dome ultrastructure.
strongestDistractor: Subendothelial tram-track deposits (MPGN), another cause of adult nephrotic syndrome with thickened basement membranes.
distractorExclusion: MPGN has subendothelial deposits and low complement; membranous nephropathy has subepithelial deposits and normal complement.

references.label: New England Journal of Medicine 2021 Pathogenesis and Treatment of Membranous Nephropathy

subject: Microbiology
topic: Angioinvasive Fungal Infections & Aspergillus vs Mucorales Morphology
shortestValidSolution: Neutropenia + halo sign + narrow septate hyphae branching at 45 degrees = Aspergillus fumigatus.
necessaryInference: Use the 45-degree acute-angle septate branching morphology to differentiate Aspergillus from right-angle non-septate Mucorales.
strongestDistractor: Rhizopus arrhizus (Mucorales), which shares angioinvasion and neutropenic risk but has broad non-septate right-angle hyphae.
distractorExclusion: Right-angle branching and lack of septations define Mucorales; 45-degree septate hyphae are diagnostic of Aspergillus.

references.label: Clinical Infectious Diseases 2021 Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Cobalamin (Vitamin B12) vs Folate Deficiency & Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase
shortestValidSolution: Macrocytic anemia + subacute combined degeneration (dorsal column/corticospinal) = B12 deficiency -> elevated methylmalonic acid and elevated homocysteine.
necessaryInference: Use the presence of neurologic deficits to identify B12 deficiency and pair it with elevated MMA (which is normal in folate deficiency).
strongestDistractor: Normal MMA and elevated homocysteine (folate deficiency), which causes identical megaloblastic anemia and hypersegmented neutrophils.
distractorExclusion: Subacute combined degeneration and elevated methylmalonic acid are unique to vitamin B12 deficiency; folate deficiency has normal MMA.

references.label: New England Journal of Medicine 2021 Vitamin B12 Deficiency: Mechanisms and Clinical Diagnosis

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Acetazolamide & Proximal Tubular Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibition
shortestValidSolution: Altitude prophylaxis + alkaline urine (pH 7.8) + metabolic acidosis + altered carbonation taste = acetazolamide -> proximal tubule carbonic anhydrase inhibition.
necessaryInference: Identify acetazolamide from the classic altitude indication and beverage taste change, then identify its proximal tubular carbonic anhydrase target.
strongestDistractor: Distal convoluted tubule NCCT inhibition (thiazides), another mild diuretic, which produces alkalosis rather than acidosis.
distractorExclusion: Thiazides cause metabolic alkalosis and acidic urine; acetazolamide causes metabolic acidosis and alkaline urine.

references.label: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology 15th ed. Chapter 15: Diuretic Agents

subject: Physiology
topic: Thyroid Autoregulation & The Wolff-Chaikoff Effect
shortestValidSolution: Amiodarone (iodine excess) causing hypothyroidism (high TSH, low free T4) = Wolff-Chaikoff effect -> inhibition of TPO organification.
necessaryInference: Distinguish the Wolff-Chaikoff effect (iodine-induced hypothyroidism via TPO blockade) from Jod-Basedow (iodine-induced hyperthyroidism).
strongestDistractor: Jod-Basedow phenomenon, the alternative iodine-related thyroid perturbation which causes hyperthyroidism instead of hypothyroidism.
distractorExclusion: Jod-Basedow produces hyperthyroidism (suppressed TSH); elevated TSH and low T4 prove Wolff-Chaikoff hypothyroidism.

references.label: Endocrine Reviews 2021 Amiodarone and the Thyroid: Clinical Practice and Mechanisms

subject: Genetics
topic: Fragile X Syndrome & FMR1 CGG Trinucleotide Repeat Hypermethylation
shortestValidSolution: Macroorchidism + large ears/long face + CGG repeat > 200 in FMR1 = DNA hypermethylation of CpG islands causing gene silencing.
necessaryInference: Connect the 5' UTR CGG expansion to the epigenetic mechanism of promoter hypermethylation and transcriptional silencing.
strongestDistractor: Polyglutamine aggregate formation (Huntington disease), which is caused by coding CAG repeats rather than 5' non-coding CGG repeats.
distractorExclusion: Huntington disease involves CAG repeats in exons; Fragile X involves non-coding CGG repeats causing methylation-induced gene silencing.

references.label: GeneReviews 2021 Fragile X Syndrome: FMR1 Genetics and Molecular Pathogenesis

subject: Anatomy
topic: Post-Ductal Coarctation of the Aorta & Intercostal Collateral Flow
shortestValidSolution: Coarctation of the aorta (upper > lower BP, radial-femoral delay) + rib notching = internal thoracic to posterior intercostal collaterals.
necessaryInference: Identify the exact vascular anastomosis (internal thoracic to posterior intercostal) responsible for costal erosion in coarctation.
strongestDistractor: Superior-inferior epigastric anastomosis, which is another major collateral pathway in coarctation but runs in the rectus sheath without touching ribs.
distractorExclusion: Epigastric collaterals run in the anterior abdominal wall; only posterior intercostal arteries traverse the subcostal grooves to erode ribs.

references.label: Circulation 2021 Management of Adults with Coarctation of the Aorta: ACC/AHA Guideline

subject: Physiology
topic: Renal Artery Stenosis & Juxtaglomerular Apparatus Hyperplasia
shortestValidSolution: Renal artery stenosis + flank bruit -> hypoperfusion causes hyperplasia of afferent arteriole juxtaglomerular cells filled with renin granules.
necessaryInference: Identify the exact cell type in the afferent arteriole (juxtaglomerular smooth muscle cells) and its secretory product (renin).
strongestDistractor: Macula densa epithelial cells, which are part of the JGA but sense NaCl rather than storing and secreting renin.
distractorExclusion: Macula densa cells are sensory epithelial cells in the distal tubule; only JG cells in the afferent arteriole store and secrete renin.

references.label: Hypertension 2021 Mechanisms and Pathophysiology of Renovascular Hypertension: The Juxtaglomerular Apparatus

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Classic Galactosemia & GALT Deficiency vs Galactokinase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Infant formula + liver failure + cataracts + positive urine reducing substances + E. coli sepsis = GALT deficiency (classic galactosemia).
necessaryInference: Distinguish GALT deficiency (liver failure, sepsis, cataracts) from GALK deficiency (isolated cataracts only).
strongestDistractor: Galactokinase (GALK) deficiency, which also causes infantile cataracts from galactitol but lacks liver failure or sepsis.
distractorExclusion: GALK deficiency is clinically benign apart from cataracts; severe liver failure and E. coli sepsis are unique to GALT deficiency.

references.label: GeneReviews 2021 Classic Galactosemia and GALT Deficiency

subject: Microbiology
topic: Listeria monocytogenes Actin Polymerization & Cell-to-Cell Spread
shortestValidSolution: Unpasteurized cheese + preterm infant death + tumbling motility at 22 C = Listeria -> ActA polymerizes host actin into "actin rockets".
necessaryInference: Identify Listeria monocytogenes and connect its intracellular propulsion directly to host actin polymerization.
strongestDistractor: Microtubule tubulin polymer networks, which are used for intracellular transport but not for bacterial actin comet propulsion.
distractorExclusion: Listeria motility relies exclusively on actin microfilaments; it does not use tubulin microtubules.

references.label: Cell Host & Microbe 2021 Listeria monocytogenes: Mechanisms of Pathogenesis and Host Invasion

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Succinylcholine Phase 1 vs Phase 2 Depolarizing Neuromuscular Blockade
shortestValidSolution: Prolonged apnea after succinylcholine + equal twitches without fade on TOF = pseudocholinesterase deficiency maintaining Phase 1 block.
necessaryInference: Connect prolonged succinylcholine paralysis with equal TOF twitches to plasma pseudocholinesterase deficiency and Phase 1 block.
strongestDistractor: Phase 2 desensitization block, which occurs after prolonged exposure and mimics non-depolarizing blockers by showing fade on TOF.
distractorExclusion: Phase 1 block exhibits NO fade (TOF ratio = 1.0); Phase 2 block displays fade and tetanic depression.

references.label: Anesthesiology 2021 Neuromuscular Monitoring and Butyrylcholinesterase Deficiency

subject: Immunology
topic: Chronic Granulomatous Disease & NADPH Oxidase gp91phox Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Burkholderia cepacia + Serratia abscesses + negative DHR flow cytometry = NADPH oxidase gp91phox defect (CGD).
necessaryInference: Connect recurrent catalase-positive infections and absent DHR oxidation to NADPH oxidase failure.
strongestDistractor: Myeloperoxidase deficiency, which affects the downstream enzyme converting H2O2 to HOCl but has a normal DHR assay.
distractorExclusion: MPO deficiency has a normal respiratory burst and normal DHR fluorescence; CGD has absent DHR fluorescence.

references.label: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology 2021 Chronic Granulomatous Disease: Pathogenesis, Genetics, and Diagnosis

subject: Pathology
topic: Dermatomyositis & Perifascicular CD4+ Muscle Atrophy
shortestValidSolution: Gottron papules + heliotrope rash + proximal weakness = dermatomyositis -> perifascicular atrophy with CD4+ perivascular inflammation.
necessaryInference: Use the cutaneous features to diagnose dermatomyositis and map to its signature perifascicular atrophy on muscle biopsy.
strongestDistractor: Endomysial CD8+ infiltrate, which describes polymyositis (lacks rash and lacks perifascicular atrophy).
distractorExclusion: Polymyositis has endomysial CD8+ infiltrates without perifascicular atrophy; dermatomyositis exhibits perimysial perifascicular atrophy.

references.label: Lancet 2021 Dermatomyositis: Clinical Features, Pathogenesis, and Malignancy Screening

subject: Genetics
topic: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 & Menin Tumor Suppressor Inactivation
shortestValidSolution: Gastrinoma + hyperparathyroidism + prolactinoma (3 Ps) = MEN 1 -> inactivating mutation in MEN1 tumor suppressor gene (menin).
necessaryInference: Identify MEN 1 from the 3 Ps and connect to inactivating MEN1 tumor suppressor mutations, distinguishing from activating RET mutations.
strongestDistractor: Activating RET proto-oncogene mutation, which causes MEN 2A/2B (medullary thyroid cancer + pheochromocytoma).
distractorExclusion: RET mutations cause MEN 2; gastrinomas and pituitary adenomas occur exclusively in MEN 1 (MEN1 gene).

references.label: Endocrine Reviews 2021 Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1: Latest Insights into Genetics and Pathogenesis

subject: Pathology
topic: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria & PIGA GPI Anchor Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Dark morning urine + Coombs-negative hemolysis + Budd-Chiari thrombosis + CD55/CD59 absence = PNH -> acquired somatic PIGA mutation.
necessaryInference: Connect intravascular hemolysis and atypical thrombosis to acquired PIGA mutation causing GPI anchor and CD55/CD59 deficiency.
strongestDistractor: JAK2 V617F mutation, another major cause of Budd-Chiari syndrome that presents with polycythemia rather than complement hemolysis and pancytopenia.
distractorExclusion: JAK2 mutations cause myeloproliferative neoplasms with elevated blood counts; PNH causes pancytopenia with CD55/CD59 deficiency.

references.label: Blood 2021 How I Treat Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria

subject: Anatomy
topic: Neurosyphilis Tabes Dorsalis & Dorsal Column Ataxia / Argyll Robertson Pupil
shortestValidSolution: Sensory ataxia (Romberg + stomping gait) + Argyll Robertson pupil (accommodates, no light reaction) = tabes dorsalis -> dorsal root/dorsal column degeneration.
necessaryInference: Recognize the classic neurosyphilis triad (dorsal column loss, sensory ataxia, Argyll Robertson pupil) and localize to dorsal roots/columns.
strongestDistractor: Lateral corticospinal tract degeneration, which causes spastic weakness and hyperreflexia rather than sensory ataxia and hyporeflexia.
distractorExclusion: Corticospinal tracts mediate motor strength and tone; tabes dorsalis specifically destroys the sensory dorsal columns with intact motor strength.

references.label: Journal of the Neurological Sciences 2021 Neurosyphilis: A Comprehensive Review of Pathophysiology and Clinical Manifestations

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Wilson Disease & ATP7B Copper-Transporting P-Type ATPase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Tremor + psychiatric changes + Kayser-Fleischer rings + low ceruloplasmin = Wilson disease -> defective ATP7B copper transporter.
necessaryInference: Connect Kayser-Fleischer rings and low ceruloplasmin to ATP7B failure in biliary copper excretion and Golgi incorporation.
strongestDistractor: ATP7A transporter defect, which causes Menkes disease (systemic copper deficiency), not copper overload.
distractorExclusion: ATP7A mutations cause Menkes kinky hair disease (copper deficiency); ATP7B mutations cause Wilson disease (copper toxicity).

references.label: Hepatology 2022 AASLD Practice Guidance on Wilson Disease

subject: Physiology
topic: Cardiac Pressure-Volume Loop Shifts in Severe Aortic Stenosis
shortestValidSolution: Aortic stenosis -> massive increase in afterload -> PV loop shows tall peak systolic pressure and increased end-systolic volume.
necessaryInference: Predict PV loop shifts in aortic stenosis: increased peak pressure and increased ESV due to high afterload.
strongestDistractor: Widening of the loop with loss of isovolumetric phases, which describes aortic regurgitation, not stenosis.
distractorExclusion: Aortic regurgitation widens the loop with no isovolumetric phases; aortic stenosis elevates peak systolic pressure and increases ESV.

references.label: Circulation 2021 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Hemodynamics

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Glycogen Storage Disease Type 1 (Von Gierke) & Glucose-6-Phosphatase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Severe fasting hypoglycemia + high lactate + high uric acid + doll facies + massive liver = glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (Von Gierke).
necessaryInference: Differentiate Von Gierke (high lactate, impaired gluconeogenesis) from Cori disease (normal lactate, intact gluconeogenesis).
strongestDistractor: Debranching enzyme deficiency (Cori disease), which also causes hypoglycemia and hepatomegaly but has normal lactate.
distractorExclusion: Cori disease has intact gluconeogenesis, so serum lactate is normal; high lactic acidosis proves glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency.

references.label: GeneReviews 2021 Glycogen Storage Disease Type I: Genetics and Metabolic Management

subject: Genetics
topic: Huntington Disease & Paternal CAG Trinucleotide Repeat Anticipation
shortestValidSolution: Huntington disease earlier onset in son (68 repeats) vs father (44 repeats) = genetic anticipation via paternal spermatogenesis CAG expansion.
necessaryInference: Connect genetic anticipation in Huntington disease specifically to repeat expansion during paternal spermatogenesis.
strongestDistractor: Expansion occurring during maternal oogenesis, which is the rule for Fragile X and Myotonic Dystrophy, not Huntington.
distractorExclusion: Huntington expands during male meiosis (spermatogenesis); maternal expansion characterizes Fragile X and Myotonic Dystrophy.

references.label: Nature Reviews Neurology 2021 Huntington's Disease: Pathogenesis and Trinucleotide Repeat Dynamics

subject: Microbiology
topic: Clostridioides difficile Toxins A and B & Rho GTPase Monoglucosylation
shortestValidSolution: Pseudomembranous colitis -> C. diff toxins A and B monoglucosylate Rho GTPases, disrupting the actin cytoskeleton.
necessaryInference: Identify Rho family GTPase monoglucosylation as the specific enzymatic mechanism of C. diff toxins A and B.
strongestDistractor: ADP-ribosylation of EF-2, which halts protein synthesis (diphtheria/Pseudomonas) but is not the C. diff mechanism.
distractorExclusion: C. diff toxins are glucosyltransferases targeting Rho GTPases; they do not ADP-ribosylate EF-2.

references.label: Nature Reviews Microbiology 2021 Mechanisms of Clostridioides difficile Toxin Pathogenesis

subject: Immunology
topic: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome & WASp Actin Cytoskeletal Assembly Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Thrombocytopenia with small platelets (low MPV) + eczema + recurrent infections = Wiskott-Aldrich -> defective actin cytoskeleton nucleation (WASp).
necessaryInference: Connect microthrombocytes and eczema to WASp-mediated actin cytoskeleton nucleation failure.
strongestDistractor: Defective lysosomal trafficking (LYST mutation, Chédiak-Higashi), which also causes immunodeficiency but has giant granules and albinism.
distractorExclusion: Chédiak-Higashi features giant cytoplasmic granules and normal/large platelets; small platelets are pathognomonic for Wiskott-Aldrich.

references.label: Journal of Clinical Immunology 2020 Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome: Actin Regulation and Clinical Spectrum

subject: Pathology
topic: Barrett Esophagus & Intestinal Metaplasia Adenocarcinoma Sequence
shortestValidSolution: Chronic GERD + salmon-pink mucosa with goblet cells = Barrett esophagus -> stratified squamous to columnar metaplasia -> risk of adenocarcinoma.
necessaryInference: Identify the exact epithelial transition (squamous to columnar) and pair with distal adenocarcinoma.
strongestDistractor: Predisposition to squamous cell carcinoma, which arises from upper/mid-esophageal squamous epithelium (associated with tobacco/alcohol, not GERD).
distractorExclusion: Barrett metaplasia gives rise to adenocarcinoma in the distal third; squamous cell carcinoma is unrelated to Barrett esophagus.

references.label: American Journal of Gastroenterology 2022 ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Barrett's Esophagus

subject: Pathology
topic: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis & Subpleural Honeycombing with Fibroblastic Foci
shortestValidSolution: Bibasilar Velcro crackles + subpleural honeycombing + fibroblastic foci = IPF -> repetitive epithelial microinjury and TGF-beta-driven myofibroblast proliferation.
necessaryInference: Recognize that IPF is driven by epithelial injury and TGF-beta-mediated fibroblastic proliferation rather than inflammatory immune complexes.
strongestDistractor: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (type IV hypersensitivity), an interstitial lung disease that features non-caseating granulomas and upper-lobe disease.
distractorExclusion: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis features poorly formed granulomas and lymphocytic bronchiolitis; IPF has fibroblastic foci and honeycombing without granulomas.

references.label: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine 2022 Diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Digoxin Toxicity & Na+/K+-ATPase Inhibition Triggered Arrhythmias
shortestValidSolution: Digoxin toxicity (xanthopsia + AV block + bidirectional PVCs) -> Na+/K+-ATPase inhibition causes intracellular Ca2+ overload and delayed afterdepolarizations.
necessaryInference: Connect Na+/K+-ATPase pump inhibition to intracellular calcium overload driving delayed afterdepolarizations and systemic hyperkalemia.
strongestDistractor: Early afterdepolarizations (EADs), which occur in long QT syndrome and Class III antiarrhythmic toxicity, whereas digoxin causes delayed afterdepolarizations.
distractorExclusion: Digoxin causes delayed afterdepolarizations (DADs) during phase 4 diastole; EADs occur during phase 2/3 repolarization in long QT.

references.label: Circulation 2021 Digoxin Toxicity: Pathophysiology, Electrocardiographic Manifestations, and Management

subject: Anatomy
topic: Psoas Major Muscle Anatomy & Retroperitoneal Abscess Extension to the Thigh
shortestValidSolution: Psoas abscess (pain on hip extension) -> tracks along psoas fascia beneath inguinal ligament to insert on lesser trochanter.
necessaryInference: Trace the anatomical path of the psoas muscle beneath the inguinal ligament into the anterior thigh.
strongestDistractor: Spread through the femoral canal, the route of femoral hernias, which lies medial to the femoral vessels, whereas psoas lies lateral.
distractorExclusion: Iliopsoas passes in the muscular lacuna lateral to the femoral sheath, not through the medial femoral canal.

references.label: Surgical and Radiologic Anatomy 2021 The Retroperitoneal Anatomy of Psoas Abscesses

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Maple Syrup Urine Disease & Branched-Chain Alpha-Ketoacid Dehydrogenase
shortestValidSolution: Sweet burnt-sugar urine + high leucine/isoleucine/valine = MSUD -> defective BCKDH complex utilizes thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP, B1).
necessaryInference: Connect the BCKDH complex to its E1 subunit cofactor, thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), and thiamine-responsive variants.
strongestDistractor: Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP, B6), which acts in the initial transamination step of BCAAs, but is not the cofactor for the BCKDH complex.
distractorExclusion: PLP is for transaminases; BCKDH is a decarboxylase requiring TPP (vitamin B1).

references.label: GeneReviews 2020 Maple Syrup Urine Disease and BCKDH Molecular Genetics

subject: Pathology
topic: Hereditary Spherocytosis & Spectrin/Ankyrin Cytoskeletal Defects
shortestValidSolution: Family history of gallstones + spherocytes + high MCHC + reduced EMA binding = hereditary spherocytosis -> ankyrin/spectrin defect causing membrane loss.
necessaryInference: Connect ankyrin/spectrin mutations to progressive membrane loss, reduced surface area-to-volume ratio, and splenic entrapment.
strongestDistractor: Complement-mediated perforation via MAC, which causes intravascular hemolysis in PNH, whereas spherocytosis is extravascular in the spleen.
distractorExclusion: Spherocytes are destroyed extravascularly by splenic macrophages; complement MAC causes intravascular lysis.

references.label: British Journal of Haematology 2021 Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Hereditary Spherocytosis

subject: Physiology
topic: High-Altitude Acclimatization & Erythrocyte 2,3-BPG Rightward Shift
shortestValidSolution: High altitude acclimatization + elevated 2,3-BPG -> stabilizes Tense state of hemoglobin -> rightward shift facilitates peripheral tissue O2 unloading.
necessaryInference: Connect elevated 2,3-BPG to T-state stabilization and rightward shift facilitating tissue oxygen unloading.
strongestDistractor: Leftward shift enhancing alveolar loading, which is intuitive for hypoxia but physiologically incorrect because 2,3-BPG shifts the curve to the right.
distractorExclusion: 2,3-BPG lowers oxygen affinity and shifts the curve to the right; a leftward shift would prevent oxygen delivery to tissues.

references.label: High Altitude Medicine & Biology 2021 Physiological Mechanisms of High-Altitude Acclimatization

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Theophylline Toxicity & Non-Selective Phosphodiesterase / Adenosine Antagonism
shortestValidSolution: Theophylline + ciprofloxacin (CYP1A2 inhibitor) -> toxic level with seizures and arrhythmias = PDE inhibition (high cAMP) + adenosine receptor antagonism.
necessaryInference: Connect theophylline's molecular mechanism (PDE inhibition + adenosine antagonism) and CYP1A2 interaction with ciprofloxacin to toxic seizures.
strongestDistractor: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor stimulation, which is the mechanism of albuterol, not the methylxanthine theophylline.
distractorExclusion: Theophylline is not a beta-2 agonist; it acts intracellularly via PDE inhibition and surface adenosine receptor antagonism.

references.label: Chest 2021 Clinical Toxicology and Pharmacology of Methylxanthines: Theophylline

subject: Physiology
topic: Prerenal Azotemia vs Acute Tubular Necrosis & Fractional Excretion of Sodium
shortestValidSolution: FENa = (12 * 2.8) / (138 * 140) * 100 = 0.17% (< 1.0%) -> intact tubules avidly reabsorbing sodium in prerenal azotemia.
necessaryInference: Execute the FENa arithmetic formula and interpret FENa < 1% as preserved tubular function in prerenal azotemia.
strongestDistractor: FENa > 2.0% due to acute tubular necrosis, the alternative form of AKI where tubular injury prevents sodium reabsorption.
distractorExclusion: High urine osmolality (640), low urine sodium (12), and calculated FENa 0.17% confirm prerenal physiology, ruling out ATN.

references.label: New England Journal of Medicine 2021 Prerenal Azotemia and Acute Tubular Necrosis: Pathophysiology and Differential Diagnosis

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency Erythrocyte Energy Failure
shortestValidSolution: Recognize chronic hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and echinocytes without Heinz bodies or spherocytes. Mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria and rely exclusively on glycolysis for ATP generation. Pyruvate kinase deficiency leads to failure of the Na+/K+ ATPase, loss of membrane deformability, and splenic red pulp macrophage destruction.
necessaryInference: Recognize chronic hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and echinocytes without Heinz bodies or spherocytes. Mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria and rely exclusively on glycolysis for ATP generation. Pyruvate kinase deficiency leads to failure of the Na+/K+ ATPase, loss of membrane deformability, and splenic red pulp macrophage destruction.
strongestDistractor: Inability to maintain reduced glutathione against endogenous oxidant stress
distractorExclusion: This describes glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, in which impaired NADPH generation through the hexose monophosphate shunt leads to oxidant-induced hemoglobin precipitation (Heinz bodies) and episodic bite cell formation, which are absent here.

references.label: Grace RF, et al. Pyruvate kinase deficiency. Lancet. 2018;391(10137):2272-2283. PMID: 29555416.

subject: Pathology
topic: Alport Syndrome Type IV Collagen Basement Membrane Defect
shortestValidSolution: Identify X-linked hematuria, family history of premature ESRD in maternal uncles, and progressive high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss. Electron microscopy reveals alternating thinning and thickening with multi-lamellation (basket-weave appearance) of the glomerular basement membrane due to COL4A5 mutations encoding the alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen.

Electron microscopy reveals alternating thinning and thickening with multi-lamellation (basket-weave appearance) of the glomerular basement membrane due to COL4A5 mutations encoding the alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen.
strongestDistractor: Subepithelial electron-dense deposits with intervening spike-like projections of basement membrane
distractorExclusion: Subepithelial humps and spike-and-dome projections characterize membranous nephropathy, which typically presents with nephrotic syndrome in adults without sensorineural hearing loss or X-linked inheritance.

references.label: Kashtan CE. Alport syndrome: an overview of phenotype and genotype. Pediatr Nephrol. 2004;19(6):604-612. PMID: 15108034.

subject: Genetics
topic: Fragile X Syndrome FMR1 Trinucleotide Repeat Epigenetics
shortestValidSolution: Recognize intellectual disability, macroorchidism, long face, large everted ears, and hypermobile joints. Caused by CGG trinucleotide expansion (>200 repeats) in the 5' untranslated region of the FMR1 gene, which triggers DNA hypermethylation of the promoter and transcriptional silencing.

Caused by CGG trinucleotide expansion (>200 repeats) in the 5' untranslated region of the FMR1 gene, which triggers DNA hypermethylation of the promoter and transcriptional silencing.
strongestDistractor: Premature stop codon generation triggering nonsense-mediated messenger RNA decay
distractorExclusion: Trinucleotide repeats in non-coding regions (like the 5' UTR of FMR1) do not alter the reading frame to generate premature stop codons; silencing occurs epigenetically via promoter hypermethylation.

references.label: Hagerman RJ, et al. Fragile X syndrome. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017;3:17065. PMID: 28960184.

subject: Immunology
topic: Guillain-Barre Syndrome Molecular Mimicry and Histopathology
shortestValidSolution: Identify acute ascending flaccid paralysis following a diarrheal illness (Campylobacter jejuni). Pathogenesis involves molecular mimicry between lipooligosaccharides (LOS) and peripheral nerve gangliosides (e.g., GM1/GD1a), resulting in endoneurial lymphocytic and macrophage infiltration with segmental demyelination.

distractorExclusion: This describes mononeuritis multiplex secondary to systemic necrotizing vasculitis (e.g., polyarteritis nodosa), which causes asymmetric, step-wise multifocal nerve infarctions rather than symmetric ascending polyradiculoneuropathy with albuminocytologic dissociation.

references.label: Willison HJ, Jacobs BC, van Doorn PA. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2016;388(10045):717-727. PMID: 26948435.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Carbon Monoxide versus Cyanide Cellular Respiration Inhibition
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish CO from cyanide toxicity. Both can occur in house fire smoke. In cyanide poisoning, cyanide binds ferric iron (Fe3+) in cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), blocking ATP production without altering hemoglobin oxygen binding; thus PaO2, SaO2, and arterial O2 content are normal, but tissue extraction fails, resulting in abnormally high mixed venous PO2 and severe lactic acidosis.
necessaryInference: Distinguish CO from cyanide toxicity. Both can occur in house fire smoke. In cyanide poisoning, cyanide binds ferric iron (Fe3+) in cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), blocking ATP production without altering hemoglobin oxygen binding; thus PaO2, SaO2, and arterial O2 content are normal, but tissue extraction fails, resulting in abnormally high mixed venous PO2 and severe lactic acidosis.
strongestDistractor: Allosteric alteration of hemoglobin causing severe leftward shifting of the dissociation curve
distractorExclusion: A leftward shift with high-affinity trapping of oxygen occurs in carbon monoxide poisoning (via binding to ferrous Fe2+ heme), but the co-oximetry carboxyhemoglobin level is normal (3%), excluding CO as the primary driver.

references.label: Hall AH, et al. Cyanide poisoning: an update on epidemiology, toxicokinetics, and medical management. Clin Toxicol. 2011;49(9):777-789. PMID: 22074360.

subject: Pathology
topic: Transfusion-Associated Hemosiderosis Myocardial Pathology
shortestValidSolution: Identify beta-thalassemia major requiring chronic transfusions leading to secondary hemochromatosis. Iron accumulation in cardiac myocytes causes dilated or restrictive cardiomyopathy. Prussian blue staining reveals blue hemosiderin granules within the perinuclear cytoplasm of cardiac myocytes.
necessaryInference: Identify beta-thalassemia major requiring chronic transfusions leading to secondary hemochromatosis. Iron accumulation in cardiac myocytes causes dilated or restrictive cardiomyopathy. Prussian blue staining reveals blue hemosiderin granules within the perinuclear cytoplasm of cardiac myocytes.
strongestDistractor: Apple-green birefringent interstitial deposits under polarized light with Congo red stain
distractorExclusion: Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence identifies cardiac amyloidosis, characterized by insoluble immunoglobulin light-chain or transthyretin fibril deposition, not iron overload.

references.label: Wood JC. Guidelines for the management of iron overload in thalassemia. Pediatr Hematol Oncol. 2014;31(4):307-316. PMID: 24707886.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Hartnup Disease Neutral Amino Acid Transporter Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize photosensitive scaly dermatitis, intermittent cerebellar ataxia, and urinary neutral aminoaciduria (tryptophan, leucine, isoleucine) without generalized Fanconi syndrome. Hartnup disease is caused by defective SLC6A19 transporter in renal proximal tubules and enterocytes, leading to niacin deficiency because tryptophan is a precursor for NAD/NADP synthesis.

Hartnup disease is caused by defective SLC6A19 transporter in renal proximal tubules and enterocytes, leading to niacin deficiency because tryptophan is a precursor for NAD/NADP synthesis.
strongestDistractor: Basolateral dibasic amino acid exchanger mediating cystine and arginine transport
distractorExclusion: Mutations in SLC3A1 or SLC7A9 disrupt the dibasic amino acid transporter (COLA: cystine, ornithine, lysine, arginine), causing cystinuria and recurrent hexagonal cystine kidney stones without pellagra or ataxia.

references.label: Broer S. Apical neutral amino acid transport in epithelial cells. Physiol Rev. 2008;88(1):249-286. PMID: 18195088.

subject: Immunology
topic: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria Complement Regulatory Proteins
shortestValidSolution: Identify Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia with nocturnal dark urine and hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome). Caused by somatic PIGA mutation in hematopoietic stem cells, preventing glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor synthesis and resulting in loss of decay-accelerating factor (CD55) and membrane attack complex inhibitor (CD59).
necessaryInference: Identify Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia with nocturnal dark urine and hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome). Caused by somatic PIGA mutation in hematopoietic stem cells, preventing glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor synthesis and resulting in loss of decay-accelerating factor (CD55) and membrane attack complex inhibitor (CD59).
strongestDistractor: Transmembrane calcium-activated phospholipid scramblase mediating phosphatidylserine externalization
distractorExclusion: Phosphatidylserine externalization is an early marker of apoptosis and platelet procoagulant activation; its deficiency is seen in Scott syndrome (bleeding disorder), not complement-mediated hemolytic thrombosis.

references.label: Brodsky RA. Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Blood. 2014;124(18):2804-2811. PMID: 25237200.

subject: Pathology
topic: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome Presynaptic Calcium Channel Autoantibodies
shortestValidSolution: Recognize proximal muscle weakness that improves with exercise, hyporeflexia, autonomic dysfunction (dry mouth, erectile dysfunction), and heavy smoking history. High-frequency repetitive nerve stimulation shows an incremental response (>100% increase in CMAP). Caused by autoantibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels, highly associated with small cell lung carcinoma.

High-frequency repetitive nerve stimulation shows an incremental response (>100% increase in CMAP). Caused by autoantibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels, highly associated with small cell lung carcinoma.
strongestDistractor: Postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the muscle motor endplate inducing complement lysis
distractorExclusion: Antibodies to postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors cause myasthenia gravis, which presents with fatigable weakness (worsening with exercise), prominent ocular/bulbar symptoms, preserved autonomic function, and decremental response on repetitive stimulation without exercise facilitation.

references.label: Titulaer MJ, et al. Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome: from clinical characteristics to therapeutic strategies. Lancet Neurol. 2011;10(12):1098-1107. PMID: 22094130.

subject: Genetics
topic: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex mTOR Pathway Hyperactivation
shortestValidSolution: Identify subependymal nodules, cortical tubers, facial angiofibromas, ash-leaf spots, and renal angiomyolipomas. Caused by loss-of-function mutations in TSC1 (hamartin) or TSC2 (tuberin), which normally form a GAP complex that hydrolyzes Rheb-GTP to Rheb-GDP. Loss of function leads to constitutive Rheb-GTP activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

Caused by loss-of-function mutations in TSC1 (hamartin) or TSC2 (tuberin), which normally form a GAP complex that hydrolyzes Rheb-GTP to Rheb-GDP. Loss of function leads to constitutive Rheb-GTP activation of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1).

distractorExclusion: HIF-1alpha stabilization occurs when the von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) ubiquitin ligase is mutated, leading to clear cell renal cell carcinomas, pheochromocytomas, and hemangioblastomas, not tuberous sclerosis.

references.label: Henske EP, et al. Tuberous sclerosis complex. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2016;2:16035. PMID: 27226234.

subject: Microbiology
topic: Cryptococcus Neoformans Polysaccharide Capsule Virulence
shortestValidSolution: Recognize subacute headache, fever, and confusion in an HIV patient with CD4 < 100/microL. CSF shows high opening pressure and narrow-based budding yeast. Mucicarmine or India ink highlights the thick glucuronoxylomannan polysaccharide capsule, which inhibits phagocytosis.

distractorExclusion: Trehalose 6,6-dimycolate (cord factor) is a glycolipid virulence factor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis that inhibits phagolysosomal fusion and induces TNF-alpha release, not a fungal capsule.

references.label: Rajasingham R, et al. Global burden of disease of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis: an updated analysis. Lancet Infect Dis. 2017;17(8):873-881. PMID: 28483415.

subject: Pathology
topic: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency Hepatic Misfolding and Emphysema
shortestValidSolution: Recognize early-onset lower lobe panacinar emphysema in a young non-smoker with hepatic dysfunction. Caused by Glu342Lys mutation in SERPINA1 (PiZZ genotype), producing misfolded AAT that polymerizes and accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum of hepatocytes (PAS-positive diastase-resistant globules), leading to low circulating levels and uninhibited neutrophil elastase destruction of lower lung acini.

distractorExclusion: Lysosomal accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and sphingomyelin occurs in Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC1/NPC2 mutations), leading to hepatosplenomegaly and vertical supranuclear gaze palsy.

references.label: Stoller JK, Aboussouan LS. A review of alpha1-antitrypsin deficiency. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2012;185(3):246-259. PMID: 21960536.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis Protein C Degradation Kinetics
shortestValidSolution: Identify acute necrotic skin lesions on the breasts/thighs within 2-5 days of initiating warfarin without heparin bridging, especially in a patient with underlying protein C deficiency. Protein C has a very short half-life (~6-8 hours) compared to factors II (prothrombin ~60-72 hrs) and X (~40 hrs), producing a transient procoagulant window where clotting factors remain active while endogenous anticoagulant protein C is depleted.

references.label: Nazarian RM, et al. Warfarin-induced skin necrosis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2009;61(2):325-332. PMID: 19615543.

subject: Genetics
topic: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2 RET Receptor Tyrosine Kinase
shortestValidSolution: Identify medullary thyroid carcinoma (calcitonin-secreting parafollicular C cells) and pheochromocytoma (chromaffin cells). Both derive from the neural crest. Caused by gain-of-function germline mutations in the RET proto-oncogene, which encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase.

subject: Immunology
topic: Hyper-IgM Syndrome CD40 Ligand Class-Switch Recombination
shortestValidSolution: Recognize recurrent sinopulmonary bacterial infections and opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis jirovecii, Cryptosporidium) in a male infant. Serum shows markedly low IgG, IgA, and IgE, with elevated or normal IgM. Caused by X-linked CD40L (CD154) deficiency on activated CD4+ T helper cells, preventing B-cell class-switch recombination and somatic hypermutation in germinal centers.

references.label: Davies EG, Thrasher AJ. Update on the hyper immunoglobulin M syndromes. Br J Haematol. 2010;149(2):167-180. PMID: 20201948.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Lithium-Induced Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus ENaC Uptake
shortestValidSolution: Identify polyuria, polydipsia, hypernatremia, and dilute urine unresponsive to desmopressin in a patient taking lithium for bipolar disorder. Lithium enters collecting duct principal cells via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC), inhibiting glycogen synthase kinase 3beta (GSK3beta) and downregulating vasopressin-induced aquaporin-2 gene expression and translocation. Amiloride treats this by competitively blocking ENaC.

Amiloride treats this by competitively blocking ENaC.

references.label: Bao H, et al. Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Am J Physiol Renal Physiol. 2012;302(6):F631-F638. PMID: 22189947.

subject: Pathology
topic: Celiac Disease Duodenal Histopathology and Transglutaminase
shortestValidSolution: Recognize chronic diarrhea, weight loss, iron deficiency anemia, and dermatitis herpetiformis. Duodenal biopsy demonstrates intraepithelial lymphocytosis, crypt hyperplasia, and villous atrophy. Tissue transglutaminase deamidates dietary gliadin, creating negatively charged peptides that bind HLA-DQ2/DQ8 on antigen-presenting cells with high affinity.

subject: Genetics
topic: Ataxia-Telangiectasia DNA Double-Strand Break Repair Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize progressive cerebellar ataxia in early childhood, conjunctival and cutaneous telangiectasias, recurrent sinopulmonary infections (IgA deficiency), elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and high sensitivity to ionizing radiation. subject: Pharmacology
topic: Methotrexate and Leucovorin Biochemical Rescue Mechanism

Leucovorin (folinic acid / N5-formyl-THF) rescues normal cells because it is converted directly to tetrahydrofolate without requiring DHFR, bypassing the blocked enzymatic step.

Succinylcholine is a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker rapidly hydrolyzed in plasma by butyrylcholinesterase (pseudocholinesterase) within 5-10 minutes. Atypical pseudocholinesterase (BCHE gene mutation, autosomal recessive) fails to hydrolyze succinylcholine, prolonging paralysis. Confirmed by low dibucaine number (dibucaine inhibits normal pseudocholinesterase by 80%, but atypical by only 20%).

subject: Immunology
topic: Immunoglobulin A Vasculitis Leukocytoclastic Postcapillary Venulitis

Follows an upper respiratory infection. Caused by galactose-deficient IgA1 immune complexes depositing in small vessels (dermal postcapillary venules and renal mesangium), producing leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Platelet count and coagulation profile are normal.

subject: Physiology
topic: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome Parietal Cell CCK-B Hyperstimulation

subject: Pathology
topic: Myasthenia Gravis Thymic Follicular Hyperplasia Pathology

Thymic pathology: Thymic lymphoid follicular hyperplasia with germinal centers is present in 65-75% of patients (thymoma in 10-15%). Thymectomy improves symptoms and can induce remission by removing autoreactive T/B-cell interactions against myoid cells.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Hereditary Fructose Intolerance Aldolase B Deficiency Mechanism
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish Hereditary Fructose Intolerance (HFI) from Essential Fructosuria. Essential fructosuria (fructokinase deficiency) is completely benign and asymptomatic, causing fructose in urine. Hereditary fructose intolerance is caused by ALDOLASE B deficiency. Fructose-1-phosphate accumulates and traps intracellular inorganic phosphate (Pi), depleting cellular ATP and inhibiting both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, producing profound hypoglycemia, vomiting, jaundice, and hepatomegaly following introduction of fruits/juice/sucrose into infant diet.

subject: Anatomy
topic: Femoral Canal Anatomy and High Hernial Incarceration Risk
shortestValidSolution: Identify femoral hernia: bulge in groin below the inguinal ligament, inferolateral to the pubic tubercle, medial to the femoral vein. More common in elderly females. The femoral ring is bounded: anteriorly by inguinal ligament, posteriorly by pectineal (Cooper's) ligament, medially by lacunar ligament, and laterally by femoral vein. Because the femoral ring has unyielding rigid fibrous borders, femoral hernias carry the highest risk of incarceration and strangulation among all groin hernias.

subject: Pathology
topic: Scleroderma Renal Crisis Endothelial Proliferation and Renin

Treatment is immediate ACE INHIBITORS (captopril). Corticosteroids are a major trigger for SRC.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Acetazolamide Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibition and Proximal RTA

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Lead Poisoning Heme Synthesis Enzymes and Basophilic Stippling
shortestValidSolution: Recognize lead poisoning (plumbism): adult worker (battery plant, radiator repair, plumbing, old paint removal) presenting with abdominal colic ("lead colic"), wrist/foot drop (radial/peroneal neuropathy), nephropathy, microcytic anemia, and lead lines on gingivae (Burton lines). Lead directly inhibits two enzymes in heme synthesis: delta-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (ALAD) and ferrochelatase, causing elevation of delta-ALA and zinc protoporphyrin. Peripheral blood smear demonstrates basophilic stippling due to lead inhibition of pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase, causing ribosomal RNA aggregation.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency Erythrocyte Glycolytic Flux Dynamics
shortestValidSolution: Deduce pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency from non-immune, non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia presenting with neonatal jaundice, splenomegaly, prominent echinocytes (burr cells), negative Coombs testing, and normal osmotic fragility. Because mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria and depend entirely on substrate-level phosphorylation via glycolysis, loss of terminal pyruvate kinase impairs ATP generation and causes rigid extravascular hemolysis. The downstream metabolic block causes upstream accumulation of glycolytic intermediates, specifically 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG). Elevated 2,3-BPG binds the central cavity of deoxyhemoglobin, stabilizing the T-state and shifting the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve to the right (increasing P50), which augments peripheral tissue oxygen extraction and provides paradoxical compensation for profound anemia.

distractorExclusion: Glucose-6-phosphate accumulates in proximal glycolytic defects such as phosphofructokinase deficiency, not in terminal pyruvate kinase deficiency where distal intermediates proximal to PEP accumulate.

references.label: Grace RF, et al. Erythrocyte pyruvate kinase deficiency: 2015 status report. Am J Hematol. 2015;90(9):825-830. PMID: 26087744.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Hartnup Disease SLC6A19 Neutral Amino Acid Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Hartnup disease: autosomal recessive mutation in SLC6A19, which encodes the apical sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter in the intestinal brush border and renal proximal convoluted tubule. Impaired absorption and reabsorption of neutral amino acids (especially TRYPTOPHAN). Tryptophan is the obligatory precursor for nicotinic acid / NAD(P)+ and serotonin synthesis. Deficiency results in pellagra-like photosensitive rash (broad-collared dermatosis), cerebellar ataxia, and neutral aminoaciduria. Differentiated from dietary pellagra by presence of massive neutral aminoaciduria with normal proline, hydroxyproline, and basic amino acids. Treatment: high-protein diet and nicotinamide supplementation.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Maple Syrup Urine Disease BCKDC Thiamine Cofactor Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD): autosomal recessive deficiency of branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDC). Degrades branched-chain amino acids (Isoleucine, Leucine, Valine - "I Love Vermont maple syrup"). BCKDC is a multi-enzyme mitochondrial complex requiring 5 cofactors: Thiamine pyrophosphate (B1), Lipoic acid, CoA (B5), FAD (B2), and NAD+ (B3) - identical to pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase. Leucine accumulation causes severe neurotoxicity (cerebral edema, seizures, dystonia, sweet burnt-sugar odor). A subset of patients responds to high-dose thiamine (vitamin B1) supplementation.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Hereditary Orotic Aciduria vs OTC Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Hereditary Orotic Aciduria from Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency: Both present with elevated urinary orotic acid. OTC deficiency is an X-linked urea cycle defect characterized by SEVERE HYPERAMMONEMIA, lethargy, encephalopathy, and BUN depletion, WITHOUT megaloblastic anemia. Hereditary Orotic Aciduria is an autosomal recessive pyrimidine synthesis defect caused by UMP SYNTHASE (orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase) deficiency, presenting with MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA refractory to B12/folate, failure to thrive, developmental delay, and NORMAL serum ammonia. Treatment: Oral URIDINE (bypasses UMP synthase).

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Phenoxybenzamine Non-Competitive Antagonist Receptor Dynamics
shortestValidSolution: Recognize phenoxybenzamine: irreversible, non-competitive, long-acting alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist. Covalently binds via an ethyleneimonium intermediate to the receptor active site. In receptor pharmacodynamics: Non-competitive (irreversible) antagonists DECREASE MAXIMAL EFFICACY (Emax shifts DOWNWARD) without necessarily altering agonist potency/EC50 at low antagonist concentrations (or shifts EC50 rightward if spare receptors are depleted). Increasing norepinephrine concentration CANNOT overcome the irreversible blockade. In contrast, competitive antagonists (phentolamine, prazosin) shift the dose-response curve to the RIGHT (increasing EC50) while maintaining Emax.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Bethanechol Muscarinic Agonism for Postoperative Urinary Retention
shortestValidSolution: Recognize bethanechol: direct-acting parasympathomimetic choline ester with selective resistance to acetylcholinesterase and quaternary amine structure (does not cross blood-brain barrier). Acts on muscarinic M3 receptors on bladder detrusor muscle, activating Gq -> Phospholipase C -> IP3/DAG -> intracellular Ca2+ release -> detrusor smooth muscle contraction and trigone/sphincter relaxation, facilitating micturition. Contraindicated in mechanical bladder outlet obstruction (e.g., BPH) or peptic ulcer disease.

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Dobutamine Inotropic Beta-1 Adrenergic Gs Adenylyl Cyclase Pathway
shortestValidSolution: Recognize dobutamine: synthetic sympathomimetic amine with predominant beta-1 > beta-2 > alpha-1 agonism. Beta-1 receptor stimulation activates Gs -> Adenylyl Cyclase -> cAMP -> Protein Kinase A (PKA). subject: Pharmacology
topic: Acetazolamide Carbonic Anhydrase Proximal Bicarbonate Wasting

subject: Pharmacology
topic: Spironolactone vs Eplerenone Steroid Receptor Cross-Reactivity

Eplerenone is a selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist with minimal affinity for androgen/progesterone receptors, lacking antiandrogenic side effects.

subject: Physiology
topic: Inulin vs PAH Clearance and Filtration Fraction Calculation
shortestValidSolution: Calculate GFR, RPF, and Filtration Fraction (FF): Inulin is freely filtered, neither reabsorbed nor secreted -> Clearance of Inulin = Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR). Para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) is freely filtered and actively secreted by proximal tubules -> Clearance of PAH = Effective Renal Plasma Flow (eRPF). True RPF = eRPF / PAH extraction ratio (~0.90). Filtration Fraction (FF) = GFR / RPF = Cinulin / CPAH. Renal Blood Flow (RBF) = RPF / (1 - Hematocrit). Clearance = (Urine conc * Urine volume) / Plasma conc.

Para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) is freely filtered and actively secreted by proximal tubules -> Clearance of PAH = Effective Renal Plasma Flow (eRPF). True RPF = eRPF / PAH extraction ratio (~0.90). strongestDistractor: GFR = 80 mL/min; RPF = 400 mL/min; Filtration Fraction = 0.20 (20%)
distractorExclusion: Incorrect calculation using wrong urine flow rate or inverted concentrations; the correct Cinulin is (160 * 1.5)/2 = 120 mL/min.

subject: Physiology
topic: Free Water Clearance Dynamics in SIADH and Diabetes Insipidus
shortestValidSolution: Understand Free Water Clearance (CH2O): CH2O = V - Cosm = V * [1 - (Uosm / Posm)]. Cosm = (Uosm * V) / Posm. When urine is hypoosmotic to plasma (Uosm < Posm, e.g., central or nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, excessive water drinking), CH2O is POSITIVE, indicating pure solute-free water excretion. When urine is hyperosmotic to plasma (Uosm > Posm, e.g., SIADH, dehydration), CH2O is NEGATIVE, meaning free water is being retained and concentrated solute is excreted (also termed negative free water clearance or solute-free water reabsorption, TcH2O).

distractorExclusion: Positive free water clearance occurs when Uosm < Posm (as in diabetes insipidus), which causes water loss and hypernatremia; here the patient has SIADH with hyponatremia and hypertonic urine.

subject: Physiology
topic: Glomerulotubular Balance and Peritubular Capillary Starling Forces
shortestValidSolution: Understand Glomerulotubular (GT) Balance: Constant percentage (~65%) of filtered fluid and sodium is reabsorbed by the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) regardless of GFR fluctuations. Driven by Starling forces in PERITUBULAR CAPILLARIES. As blood traverses glomerular capillaries, fluid is filtered while plasma proteins remain, concentrating proteins in the efferent arteriole. Thus, peritubular capillaries have HIGH ONCOTIC PRESSURE (pi-c) and LOW HYDROSTATIC PRESSURE (Pc). High pi-c and low Pc create a powerful net absorptive pressure that sucks fluid and Na+ from the lateral intercellular space into peritubular capillaries. When Filtration Fraction (FF = GFR/RPF) increases (e.g., efferent arteriolar constriction), pi-c rises further, boosting proximal reabsorption.

subject: Immunology
topic: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency IL-2RG Common Gamma Chain
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID): recurrent severe viral, fungal (Candida, Pneumocystis), and bacterial infections, failure to thrive, absent thymic shadow, and chronic diarrhea in early infancy. Most common form is X-linked SCID (~50%), caused by mutation in the IL2RG gene encoding the COMMON GAMMA (gamma-c) CHAIN shared by cytokine receptors for IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, and IL-21. Defective IL-7 receptor halts T-cell development (absent T cells). Defective IL-15 receptor halts NK-cell development (absent NK cells). B cells are present in normal numbers but non-functional due to lack of T-cell help (T- B+ NK- phenotype). Signals via JAK3. In contrast, autosomal recessive Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes toxic dATP accumulation, killing all lymphocytes (T- B- NK- phenotype).

subject: Immunology
topic: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome WASP Actin Cytoskeleton Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS): X-linked recessive triad of Microthrombocytopenia (small platelets and low platelet count, bleeding/petechiae), Eczema, and Recurrent pyogenic infections. Defective actin polymerization impairs leukocyte motility, immunologic synapse formation, and platelet budding/fragmentation from megakaryocytes, producing abnormally small platelets (low mean platelet volume, MPV). Differentiated from ITP where platelets are abnormally large.

subject: Immunology
topic: Hyper-IgM Syndrome CD40L Class-Switch Recombination Failure
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Hyper-IgM Syndrome: X-linked recessive mutation in CD40LG (CD154) on activated CD4+ T helper cells. CD40L normally binds CD40 on B cells, providing the obligatory second costimulatory signal for activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) expression and immunoglobulin heavy-chain class-switch recombination (CSR) from IgM/IgD to IgG, IgA, and IgE. Failure of CSR results in markedly elevated or normal serum IgM with undetectable/profoundly low IgG, IgA, and IgE. Crucially, CD40L-CD40 interaction is also required for macrophage activation (via IFN-gamma priming); lack of CD40L impairs cell-mediated immunity, causing opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, Cryptosporidium parvum biliary disease), distinguishing it from pure B-cell agammaglobulinemia.

subject: Immunology
topic: Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type 1 CD18 Beta-2 Integrin Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type 1 (LAD-1): autosomal recessive mutation in ITGB2 (CD18), the beta-2 subunit of integrins (LFA-1 [CD11a/CD18] and Mac-1 [CD11b/CD18]). Integrins mediate TIGHT ADHESION and stable arrest of neutrophils to endothelial ICAM-1 (CD54) during leukocyte extravasation. Hallmarks: 1. Delayed detachment/separation of the umbilical cord (> 30 days; normal is 1-2 weeks); 2. Recurrent necrotic skin and mucosal bacterial/fungal infections WITHOUT PUS formation (neutrophils cannot migrate into tissues); 3. Persistent, profound neutrophilic LEUKOCYTOSIS (> 30,000-100,000/microL) because neutrophils cannot marginate into tissues. Differentiated from LAD-2 which is caused by defective fucose metabolism (absence of Sialyl-Lewis X, affecting rolling).

subject: Immunology
topic: Chediak-Higashi Syndrome LYST Lysosomal Trafficking Defect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Chédiak-Higashi syndrome: autosomal recessive mutation in the LYST gene (lysosomal trafficking regulator). Recurrent pyogenic staphylococcal/streptococcal infections (impaired phagolysosome killing); 3. Progressive peripheral and cranial neuropathies; 4. Bleeding diathesis (dense platelet granule defect). Peripheral blood smear is pathognomonic: GIANT AZUROPHILIC LYSOSOMAL GRANULES within neutrophils, monocytes, and eosinophils.

subject: Genetics
topic: Ataxia-Telangiectasia ATM Gene Non-Homologous End Joining
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Ataxia-Telangiectasia: autosomal recessive mutation in the ATM gene on chromosome 11q22. Extreme hypersensitivity to IONIZING RADIATION and high risk of hematologic malignancies (lymphoma/leukemia).

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Alkaptonuria Homogentisate 1,2-Dioxygenase Ochronosis
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Alkaptonuria: autosomal recessive defect in homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase in the degradative pathway of tyrosine to fumarate. Homogentisic acid (HGA) accumulates and is excreted in urine. HGA oxidizes to a dark pigment when urine stands or is exposed to air/alkali. Pigment polymerizes and deposits in connective tissue (OCHRONOSIS): bluish-black pigmentation of sclerae, ear cartilage, and heart valves. In adults (ages 30-50), pigment binds collagen in joints and intervertebral discs, causing dense disc calcification, loss of lumbar lordosis, and crippling debilitating osteoarthropathy (ankylosis of spine and large joints). Benign in childhood aside from dark urine in diapers.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Cystinuria COLA Transporter Defect and Hexagonal Crystals
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Cystinuria: autosomal recessive defect in the apical sodium-independent dibasic amino acid transporter (rBAT / SLC3A1 and b0,+AT / SLC7A9) in renal proximal tubules and small intestine. Prevents reabsorption of COLA: Cystine, Ornithine, Lysine, Arginine. Only CYSTINE is poorly soluble in acidic urine (pH < 7.0), causing recurrent nephrolithiasis in young patients (teens/20s). Urinalysis shows pathognomonic flat, colorless, HEXAGONAL crystals. Treatment: aggressive hydration, urinary alkalinization (potassium citrate/bicarbonate to pH > 7.5), and chelating agents (tiopronin/penicillamine) for refractory stones.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Glycogen Storage Disease Type I Glucose-6-Phosphatase
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Glycogen Storage Disease Type I (von Gierke disease): autosomal recessive deficiency of Glucose-6-Phosphatase (Type Ia) or G6P translocase (Type Ib). Hyperlipidemia (excess G6P shunted to acetyl-CoA -> triglycerides/cholesterol -> xanthomas, doll-like cherubic facies); 5. Massive hepatomegaly with NORMAL spleen (glycogen accumulates in liver). Treatment: frequent oral uncooked cornstarch and avoidance of fructose/galactose (which cannot be converted to free glucose).

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Glycogen Storage Disease Type V Myophosphorylase Deficiency
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Glycogen Storage Disease Type V (McArdle disease): autosomal recessive deficiency of skeletal muscle glycogen phosphorylase (myophosphorylase / PYGM). Exercise intolerance, severe painful muscle cramps, and fatigue during intense, short bursts of anaerobic exercise; 2. "Second-wind" phenomenon (after ~10 minutes of rest or reduced exertion, heart rate drops and exercise tolerance improves because blood-borne substrates like fatty acids and liver-derived glucose reach muscles); 3. Rhabdomyolysis and myoglobinuria (red-brown urine after exertion, positive dipstick blood with 0 RBCs, acute tubular necrosis risk); 4. Non-ischemic forearm exercise test reveals FLAT VENOUS LACTATE CURVE with normal or exaggerated rise in venous ammonia.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase II Deficiency Rhabdomyolysis
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase II (CPT II) deficiency from glycogen storage diseases: CPT II deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder of the carnitine shuttle (catalyzes the reformation of acyl-carnitine into acyl-CoA inside the mitochondrial matrix). Most common adult form presents with recurrent exercise-, cold-, infection-, or fasting-induced RHABDOMYOLYSIS, myoglobinuria, and muscle pain, without the "second-wind" phenomenon of McArdle disease. Because long-chain fatty acids cannot enter the mitochondrial matrix for beta-oxidation, acetyl-CoA is depleted, preventing hepatic ketone body synthesis during fasting. This produces HYPOKETOTIC HYPOGLYCEMIA during prolonged fasting (in contrast to normal ketones/glycogenolysis in pure muscle glycogenoses). Muscle biopsy reveals lipid droplet accumulation in type I slow-twitch muscle fibers.

subject: Biochemistry
topic: Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency Hypoketotic Hypoglycemia

Hepatic dysfunction (hyperammonemia, elevated transaminases, hepatomegaly with microvesicular steatosis); 4. subject: Genetics
topic: Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 CTG Trinucleotide Repeat DMPK Defect

subject: Genetics
topic: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 Menin Tumor Suppressor

topic: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2A RET Proto-Oncogene

subject: Physiology
topic: Primary Hyperaldosteronism Aldosterone Escape Mechanism
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Primary Hyperaldosteronism (Conn Syndrome): aldosterone-producing adrenal adenoma (~60%) or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (~40%). Triad of: 1. Treatment-resistant HYPERTENSION; 2. HYPOKALEMIA (muscle weakness, cramps, paresthesias); 3. METABOLIC ALKALOSIS (aldosterone stimulates H+-ATPase in type A intercalated cells). Renin is markedly suppressed (Aldosterone-to-Renin Ratio ARR > 20-30). CRUCIAL PHYSIOLOGICAL PHENOMENON: PATIENTS DO NOT DEVELOP SIGNIFICANT PERIPHERAL EDEMA ("ALDOSTERONE ESCAPE"). Unregulated aldosterone initially causes Na+ and water retention, expanding extracellular fluid volume. This volume expansion triggers two homeostatic rescue mechanisms: 1. Increased stretch of cardiac atria releases ATRIAL NATRIURETIC PEPTIDE (ANP), which promotes renal sodium excretion and inhibits renin; 2. Elevated mean arterial pressure directly drives PRESSURE NATRIURESIS and pressure diuresis in renal tubules, increasing urinary Na+ excretion until Na+ intake matches output, stabilizing volume and preventing overt edema.

topic: Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia CaSR Loss-of-Function
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia (FHH) from Primary Hyperparathyroidism (PHPT): Both present with hypercalcemia and normal or mildly elevated intact PTH. In the parathyroid glands: CaSR requires higher serum calcium to suppress PTH release (calcium set-point shifted rightward). In the kidney (thick ascending limb): defective CaSR increases tubular calcium and magnesium reabsorption. CRUCIAL DECISIVE TEST: 24-HOUR URINE CALCIUM EXCRETION AND CALCIUM-TO-CREATININE CLEARANCE RATIO (CCCR): In FHH, CCCR is < 0.01 (VERY LOW urinary calcium excretion, < 100 mg/day). In Primary Hyperparathyroidism, filtered calcium load overwhelms tubular reabsorption, so urine calcium is ELEVATED (CCCR > 0.02, urine Ca > 200-300 mg/day). FHH is completely BENIGN and ASYMPTOMATIC; parathyroidectomy is INEFFECTIVE and contraindicated.

topic: Kallmann Syndrome GnRH Olfactory Neuron Migration Failure

HYPOGONADOTROPIC HYPOGONADISM (delayed or absent puberty, microphallus and cryptorchidism in infancy, low testosterone, low LH, low FSH); 2. ANOSMIA or HYPOSMIA (complete inability to perceive odors / taste flavors due to hypoplastic or absent olfactory bulbs and tracts). subject: Pathology
topic: Craniopharyngioma Rathke Pouch Adamantinomatous Pathology
