subject: Medicine
topic: Post-MI Ventricular Septal Rupture vs Mitral Regurgitation
shortestValidSolution: Post-MI shock on day 4 + harsh murmur with thrill + RA-to-RV O2 step-up (64% to 84%) = ventricular septal rupture -> IABP afterload reduction + emergency surgery.
necessaryInference: Interpret hemodynamic O2 saturation step-up to differentiate VSR from papillary muscle rupture and free wall rupture.
strongestDistractor: Acute papillary muscle rupture, which shares cardiogenic shock and pulmonary edema post-MI but lacks a thrill and has NO oxygen step-up.
distractorExclusion: The RV oxygen saturation step-up from 64% to 84% definitively proves left-to-right shunting at the ventricular level.

references.label: 2025 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes

subject: Medicine
topic: Severe Acute Pancreatitis & ARDS Ventilator Management
shortestValidSolution: Severe ARDS (P/F 80) on 6 mL/kg PBW -> increase PEEP to recruit alveoli while maintaining low tidal volumes.
necessaryInference: Recognize that hypoxemia in ARDS is treated by escalating PEEP, not by increasing tidal volume (which increases mortality).
strongestDistractor: Increasing tidal volume to correct pH 7.28, a classic trap that violates ARDSNet low tidal volume guidelines.
distractorExclusion: High tidal volumes increase alveolar strain and mortality; permissive hypercapnia is accepted to protect the lungs.

references.label: ESICM 2023 Guidelines on Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Variceal Bleeding & Restrictive Transfusion Strategy
shortestValidSolution: Acute variceal bleed -> IV octreotide + IV ceftriaxone + restrictive transfusion (Hb < 7 g/dL) prior to emergent endoscopy.
necessaryInference: Recognize the tri-part medical therapy (octreotide, ceftriaxone, restrictive transfusion threshold < 7 g/dL) and avoid beta-blockers in acute hemorrhage.
strongestDistractor: Liberal blood transfusion to target Hb > 10 g/dL, which is intuitive but proven to increase portal pressure and rebleeding mortality.
distractorExclusion: Clinical trials demonstrate that liberal transfusion worsens portal hypertension; restrictive transfusion (Hb < 7) improves survival.

references.label: AASLD Practice Guidance 2024: Portal Hypertension and Variceal Bleeding

subject: Medicine
topic: Community-Acquired Bacterial Meningitis & Dexamethasone Prior to Antibiotics
shortestValidSolution: Meningitis signs + age 58 -> IV dexamethasone with vancomycin + ceftriaxone + ampicillin immediately.
necessaryInference: Recognize that dexamethasone must be administered prior to or concurrently with antibiotics, and include ampicillin for patients >= 50.
strongestDistractor: Perform head CT prior to LP/antibiotics, a frequent error that delays critical antimicrobial administration.
distractorExclusion: No papilledema or focal deficits are present, so CT is not required before LP; antibiotics must never be delayed for imaging.

references.label: IDSA Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis

subject: Surgery
topic: Blunt Abdominal Trauma & Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (FAST)
shortestValidSolution: Unstable blunt trauma (BP 84/50) + positive FAST (free fluid) = immediate exploratory laparotomy.
necessaryInference: Connect persistent shock + free fluid on FAST directly to emergency laparotomy, rejecting CT.
strongestDistractor: Transfer to helical abdominal CT, which is the standard workup for stable trauma patients.
distractorExclusion: CT requires hemodynamic stability; sending an actively hemorrhaging unstable patient to CT risks fatal decompensation.

references.label: ATLS Advanced Trauma Life Support 10th ed. Chapter 5: Abdominal and Pelvic Trauma

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Biliary Atresia & Direct Hyperbilirubinemia Diagnostic Workup
shortestValidSolution: 4-week-old with direct hyperbilirubinemia + acholic stools = biliary atresia -> initial test: RUQ ultrasound.
necessaryInference: Recognize direct (conjugated) hyperbilirubinemia as an emergency requiring structural biliary imaging (ultrasound), not phototherapy.
strongestDistractor: Phototherapy, the standard treatment for neonatal jaundice, which is only used for unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
distractorExclusion: Phototherapy is ineffective for conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and causes bronze baby syndrome; anatomic biliary evaluation is mandatory.

references.label: NASPGHAN/ESPGHAN Guidelines for the Evaluation of Cholestatic Jaundice in Infants

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Postpartum Hemorrhage & Uterotonic Selection Contraindications
shortestValidSolution: Uterine atony bleeding + severe asthma -> carboprost is contraindicated -> give intramuscular methylergonovine (patient is not hypertensive).
necessaryInference: Identify patient-specific contraindication (asthma contraindicates carboprost) to select methylergonovine.
strongestDistractor: Carboprost tromethamine (PGF2-alpha), the standard second-line uterotonic, which is lethal in severe asthma due to bronchoconstriction.
distractorExclusion: Carboprost induces severe bronchospasm; asthma is an absolute contraindication.

references.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Bipolar I Disorder Acute Manic Episode Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Acute mania (Bipolar I) -> atypical antipsychotic (quetiapine/olanzapine) or lithium/valproate; avoid SSRIs.
necessaryInference: Recognize acute mania and choose a second-generation antipsychotic/mood stabilizer while rejecting antidepressant triggers.
strongestDistractor: Lamotrigine, a common bipolar medication, which is ineffective for acute mania and carries SJS risk with fast titration.
distractorExclusion: Lamotrigine treats bipolar depression, not mania; atypical antipsychotics or lithium/valproate are required for acute mania.

references.label: American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Bipolar Disorder

subject: Medicine
topic: Severe Symptomatic Hyponatremia & Hypertonic Saline Rate Correction Limits
shortestValidSolution: Hyponatremic seizure (Na 112) -> 3% hypertonic saline boluses; maximum 24-hour rise is <= 8 mEq/L to prevent osmotic demyelination.
necessaryInference: Select hypertonic saline for seizures and apply the evidence-based 8 mEq/L 24-hour correction ceiling.
strongestDistractor: 0.9% normal saline with a 15-20 mEq/L target, an outdated and dangerous practice that triggers central pontine myelinolysis.
distractorExclusion: A rise > 8 mEq/L in 24 hours causes irreversible osmotic demyelination; 3% NaCl boluses with strict limits are required.

references.label: American Journal of Kidney Diseases 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyponatremia

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Kawasaki Disease Diagnosis & Prevention of Coronary Artery Aneurysms
shortestValidSolution: Fever >= 5 days + strawberry tongue + conjunctivitis + red hands/feet + adenopathy = Kawasaki disease -> IVIG (2 g/kg) + aspirin + echocardiogram.
necessaryInference: Identify Kawasaki disease from clinical criteria and prioritize IVIG + aspirin within 10 days to prevent coronary aneurysms.
strongestDistractor: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate for suspected cervical adenitis, which fails to treat vasculitis and risks coronary aneurysm.
distractorExclusion: Kawasaki disease is non-bacterial; delaying IVIG beyond day 10 substantially increases the risk of giant coronary aneurysms.

references.label: Circulation 2021 Diagnosis, Treatment, and Long-Term Management of Kawasaki Disease: AHA Guideline

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Medical Stabilization & Surgical Indication
shortestValidSolution: Type A aortic dissection (chest pain + pulse deficit + wide mediastinum) -> IV beta-blocker (labetalol) first to drop HR < 60 and SBP 100-120.
necessaryInference: Recognize that beta-blockade must precede or accompany vasodilators to minimize aortic shear stress (dP/dt).
strongestDistractor: Sodium nitroprusside alone, an intuitive BP-lowering agent that causes reflex tachycardia and accelerates aortic rupture.
distractorExclusion: Pure vasodilators without beta-blockade increase dP/dt and worsen dissection; beta-blockers are mandatory first.

references.label: ACC/AHA 2022 Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Appendicitis in Pregnancy & Graded Compression Ultrasound
shortestValidSolution: Pregnant female + RUQ pain/fever/leukocytosis = appendicitis -> initial test: graded compression ultrasound (MRI if equivocal).
necessaryInference: Identify atypical anatomical location of appendicitis in pregnancy and select ultrasound followed by MRI to protect the fetus from radiation.
strongestDistractor: Immediate abdominopelvic CT scan, the gold standard in non-pregnant adults that exposes the fetus to ionizing radiation.
distractorExclusion: Ultrasound and MRI are safe in pregnancy and must be utilized before considering CT with ionizing radiation.

references.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 211: Critical Care in Pregnancy / Non-Obstetric Surgery

subject: Medicine
topic: TTP Diagnosis & Emergency Therapeutic Plasma Exchange
shortestValidSolution: Schistocytes + platelets 14k + normal PT/INR + fluctuating confusion = TTP -> immediate therapeutic plasma exchange; avoid platelets.
necessaryInference: Differentiate TTP from DIC (normal PT/INR) and initiate emergent plasmapheresis while recognizing the contraindication to platelet transfusion.
strongestDistractor: Immediate platelet transfusion, an intuitive reflex for platelets of 14,000 that causes fatal thrombosis in TTP.
distractorExclusion: Transfusing platelets in TTP adds substrate to ultra-large vWF multimers, precipitating fatal strokes and MIs.

references.label: Blood 2020 International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of TTP

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Tetralogy of Fallot & Hypercyanotic "Tet" Spell Pathophysiology and Management
shortestValidSolution: Tet spell -> knee-chest position increases SVR (afterload) -> reduces right-to-left VSD shunt -> increases pulmonary blood flow.
necessaryInference: Connect knee-chest position to increased SVR and shunt reversal rather than a primary pulmonary or vagal effect.
strongestDistractor: Decreasing right ventricular afterload, which is desired but achieved pharmacologically, whereas knee-chest physically increases systemic afterload.
distractorExclusion: Knee-chest positioning mechanically increases systemic vascular resistance by kinking femoral arteries.

references.label: Circulation 2021 Management of Congenital Heart Disease: Tetralogy of Fallot Spells

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Preeclampsia with Severe Features & Magnesium Neuroprotection / Delivery Timing
shortestValidSolution: Severe preeclampsia (BP 168/112 + headache + low platelets) at 35 weeks -> IV magnesium sulfate + IV labetalol + proceed with delivery.
necessaryInference: Identify severe features and apply the 34-week delivery threshold rather than attempting expectant management.
strongestDistractor: Expectant management until 37 or 39 weeks, which is only appropriate for gestational hypertension or preeclampsia WITHOUT severe features.
distractorExclusion: Severe features at 35 weeks mandate delivery; continuing the pregnancy risks maternal intracerebral hemorrhage and eclampsia.

references.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia

subject: Surgery
topic: Tension Pneumothorax & Immediate Needle Decompression before Imaging
shortestValidSolution: Trauma + hypotension (72/42) + absent breath sounds + tracheal deviation = tension pneumothorax -> immediate needle decompression.
necessaryInference: Recognize that tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis requiring immediate needle decompression without waiting for X-ray.
strongestDistractor: Obtaining portable chest radiograph, a frequent exam trap that delays life-saving decompression in an unstable patient.
distractorExclusion: Any delay for imaging in a patient with BP 72/42 mmHg and tension pneumothorax leads to cardiac arrest.

references.label: ATLS Advanced Trauma Life Support 10th ed. Chapter 4: Thoracic Trauma

subject: Medicine
topic: Clostridioides difficile Infection & Fidaxomicin vs Oral Vancomycin
shortestValidSolution: Initial C. difficile colitis -> oral fidaxomicin (preferred) or oral vancomycin (acceptable alternative).
necessaryInference: Apply updated IDSA guideline preference for fidaxomicin/vancomycin and reject obsolete metronidazole.
strongestDistractor: Oral metronidazole, the historical board-exam answer that has been superseded by fidaxomicin/vancomycin.
distractorExclusion: Guidelines demoted metronidazole due to high failure rates; fidaxomicin and vancomycin are superior.

references.label: Clinical Infectious Diseases 2021 IDSA/SHEA Focused Update: Management of Clostridioides difficile Infection

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Ileocolic Intussusception & Pneumatic / Hydrostatic Enema Reduction
shortestValidSolution: Infant drawing legs to chest + sausage mass + currant jelly stool + target sign = intussusception -> pneumatic (air) enema reduction.
necessaryInference: Recognize that pneumatic enema is therapeutic as well as diagnostic, avoiding premature surgery.
strongestDistractor: Immediate exploratory laparotomy, which is reserved for bowel perforation or peritonitis.
distractorExclusion: In the absence of peritonitis, pneumatic enema has an 85-90% success rate and avoids general anesthesia and surgery.

references.label: Pediatrics in Review 2021 Intussusception: Diagnosis and Management

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Unruptured Ectopic Pregnancy & Medical Methotrexate Eligibility Criteria
shortestValidSolution: Unruptured ectopic (beta-hCG 2,400, mass 2.4 cm, stable, no fetal heartbeat) -> IM methotrexate single-dose; check hCG on days 4 and 7.
necessaryInference: Verify all 5 ACOG eligibility criteria to select medical methotrexate therapy over invasive laparoscopic surgery.
strongestDistractor: Immediate laparoscopic salpingectomy, which is effective but unnecessary and invasive in an eligible candidate for methotrexate.
distractorExclusion: Stable patient with beta-hCG < 5,000 and mass < 3.5 cm meets criteria for non-surgical methotrexate therapy.

references.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 193: Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Antipsychotic-Induced Acute Dystonia & Anticholinergic Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Haloperidol + torticollis + oculogyric crisis = acute dystonia -> give IM/IV benztropine or diphenhydramine.
necessaryInference: Identify acute dystonia from involuntary eye/neck muscle contractions and distinguish from NMS and akathisia to select anticholinergic therapy.
strongestDistractor: Oral propranolol, which is the first-line treatment for akathisia (motor restlessness), not acute muscle spasms.
distractorExclusion: Propranolol treats akathisia; acute dystonic muscle spasm requires muscarinic blockade with benztropine or diphenhydramine.

references.label: American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia & CT Mesenteric Angiography
shortestValidSolution: AF + sudden severe pain out of proportion to exam + high lactate = acute mesenteric ischemia -> CT mesenteric angiography.
necessaryInference: Recognize pain out of proportion to exam with an embolic risk factor and select CT mesenteric angiography.
strongestDistractor: Colonoscopy, which evaluates colonic ischemia (watershed areas), but fails to assess small bowel mesenteric arterial occlusion.
distractorExclusion: Mesenteric ischemia affects the small bowel supplied by the SMA; colonoscopy cannot visualize the small intestine.

references.label: Journal of Vascular Surgery 2021 Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Management of Acute Mesenteric Ischemia

subject: Medicine
topic: Diabetic Ketoacidosis & Potassium Replacement Prior to Insulin Administration
shortestValidSolution: DKA + potassium 2.9 mEq/L -> withhold insulin, give IV potassium until K+ > 3.3 mEq/L, then start insulin.
necessaryInference: Recognize the critical safety contraindication: never give insulin when potassium is < 3.3 mEq/L in DKA.
strongestDistractor: Immediate IV insulin bolus, the standard reflex in DKA that is lethal when potassium is below 3.3 mEq/L.
distractorExclusion: Starting insulin before correcting K+ < 3.3 causes catastrophic intracellular potassium shifting and cardiac arrest.

references.label: Diabetes Care 2021 Management of Hyperglycemic Emergencies in Adults: ADA Consensus Statement

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Appendicitis & Clinical Diagnosis with Peritonitis Direct Laparoscopy
shortestValidSolution: Young male + classic migrating pain to McBurney point + peritonitis + leukocytosis = clinical appendicitis -> pre-op antibiotics + appendectomy.
necessaryInference: Recognize that imaging is not mandatory in young males with classic physical findings of appendicitis and peritonitis.
strongestDistractor: Triple-contrast CT scan, which is standard in atypical cases or females but unnecessary in classic young male presentations.
distractorExclusion: Classic presentation in young males has > 95% specificity; CT delays surgery and adds unnecessary radiation.

references.label: World Journal of Emergency Surgery 2020 WSES Jerusalem Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Acute Appendicitis

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Septic Arthritis of the Pediatric Hip & Kocher Criteria / Urgent Arthrocentesis
shortestValidSolution: Refusal to bear weight + fever 38.8 C + high WBC/ESR (all 4 Kocher criteria) + hip effusion = septic arthritis -> urgent arthrocentesis.
necessaryInference: Apply Kocher criteria to identify high-probability septic arthritis and prioritize emergent arthrocentesis over conservative transient synovitis management.
strongestDistractor: Oral ibuprofen and discharge for transient synovitis, which leads to permanent femoral head avascular necrosis in true septic arthritis.
distractorExclusion: Meeting all 4 Kocher criteria gives > 93% likelihood of septic arthritis, mandating immediate aspiration.

references.label: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery 2020 Differentiating Septic Arthritis from Transient Synovitis of the Hip

subject: Medicine
topic: Patient Autonomy & Informed Refusal with Intact Capacity
shortestValidSolution: Competent adult Jehovah's Witness refusing blood transfusion with understanding of death -> honor refusal, document capacity, provide non-blood resuscitation.
necessaryInference: Recognize that patient autonomy with intact decision-making capacity supersedes family demands and beneficence.
strongestDistractor: Administering blood under emergency implied consent, which is illegal and unethical when a patient has expressed competent refusal.
distractorExclusion: Implied consent is invalid when an alert, competent patient expressly refuses treatment.

references.label: AMA Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 2.1.1: Informed Consent and Refusal of Treatment

subject: Medicine
topic: HFrEF Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy & Quadruple Regimen Initiation
shortestValidSolution: HFrEF (EF 28%) on loop diuretic + beta-blocker -> add remaining foundational GDMT: ARNI + SGLT2i + spironolactone.
necessaryInference: Recognize the modern standard of care: prompt quadruple GDMT initiation rather than slow historical monotherapy titration.
strongestDistractor: Escalating furosemide to reduce neurohormonal activation, which treats symptoms but provides no mortality benefit.
distractorExclusion: Loop diuretics have no mortality benefit; ARNI, MRA, and SGLT2 inhibitors are life-saving pillars.

references.label: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure: Core Medical Therapy

subject: Medicine
topic: Primary Spontaneous Pneumothorax Management: Large vs Small Thresholds
shortestValidSolution: Large stable primary spontaneous pneumothorax (3.2 cm apex, 2.4 cm hilum) -> percutaneous needle aspiration or pigtail catheter (<= 14 Fr).
necessaryInference: Apply size criteria (>= 2 cm hilum / >= 3 cm apex) to select active catheter evacuation over conservative observation in a stable patient.
strongestDistractor: Immediate emergent needle thoracostomy, the emergency treatment for tension pneumothorax, which is inappropriate for a stable patient.
distractorExclusion: Tension pneumothorax involves hemodynamic shock and tracheal deviation; this patient is stable with normal blood pressure.

references.label: Chest 2021 Management of Spontaneous Pneumothorax: An American College of Chest Physicians Guideline

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Cholangitis (Reynolds Pentad) & Emergent ERCP Biliary Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Charcot triad + shock + confusion (Reynolds pentad) + dilated CBD = acute cholangitis -> emergent ERCP biliary decompression.
necessaryInference: Recognize that acute cholangitis requires emergent mechanical biliary decompression (ERCP), not immediate cholecystectomy.
strongestDistractor: Immediate open cholecystectomy, which treats acute cholecystitis but fails to relieve common bile duct obstruction in cholangitis.
distractorExclusion: Cholecystectomy does not remove the obstructing common bile duct calculus; ERCP is required to decompress the biliary tree.

references.label: Journal of Hepato-Biliary-Pancreatic Sciences 2018 Tokyo Guidelines 2018: Diagnostic Criteria and Severity Grading of Acute Cholangitis

subject: Medicine
topic: Contrast-Associated AKI Prevention & Isotonic Crystalloid Hydration
shortestValidSolution: High-risk CKD undergoing contrast angiography -> prevent CA-AKI with IV isotonic saline hydration; NAC is ineffective (PRESERVE trial).
necessaryInference: Incorporate the PRESERVE trial evidence disproving N-acetylcysteine and prioritize isotonic saline hydration.
strongestDistractor: Oral N-acetylcysteine, an older board favorite that was definitively proven ineffective in the PRESERVE trial.
distractorExclusion: The PRESERVE trial proved NAC is equivalent to placebo; IV saline hydration is the sole evidence-based preventive therapy.

references.label: New England Journal of Medicine 2018 Outcomes after Angiography with Sodium Bicarbonate and Acetylcysteine (PRESERVE Trial)

subject: Medicine
topic: Infective Endocarditis & Emergency Valve Surgery Indications (AHA/ACC)
shortestValidSolution: S. aureus endocarditis + acute aortic regurgitation + pulmonary edema = Class 1 indication for emergent surgical valve replacement.
necessaryInference: Recognize acute heart failure as an absolute indication for emergency cardiac surgery in infective endocarditis.
strongestDistractor: Completing 6 weeks of IV antibiotics before surgery, an outdated approach that leads to fatal heart failure decompensation.
distractorExclusion: Medical therapy alone for endocarditis with acute severe regurgitation and pulmonary edema carries prohibitive mortality; early surgery is life-saving.

references.label: Circulation 2021 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients with Valvular Heart Disease: Infective Endocarditis

subject: Medicine
topic: Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia in Adults: Corticosteroid First-Line Therapy
shortestValidSolution: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia (11,000/mcL) in adult with petechiae/bleeding -> first-line oral corticosteroids; avoid platelet transfusion.
necessaryInference: Recognize adult ITP treatment threshold (< 30,000/mcL) requiring corticosteroids and distinguish from pediatric expectant management or emergency platelet transfusion.
strongestDistractor: Prophylactic platelet transfusion, which is intuitive to novices but ineffective due to antibody-mediated destruction.
distractorExclusion: Transfused platelets are cleared by autoantibodies within minutes in ITP; platelet transfusion is reserved strictly for life-threatening bleeding.

references.label: Blood Advances 2019 American Society of Hematology 2019 Guidelines for Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)

subject: Medicine
topic: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Surgical Parathyroidectomy Indications
shortestValidSolution: Asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism in a 46-year-old with Ca 11.4 mg/dL -> age < 50 and Ca > 1.0 mg/dL above normal = parathyroidectomy.
necessaryInference: Recognize guideline thresholds for parathyroidectomy in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism (age < 50).
strongestDistractor: Expectant monitoring with annual labs, which ignores that age < 50 mandates surgical cure to prevent long-term complications.
distractorExclusion: Guidelines explicitly recommend surgery in patients < 50 years to prevent decades of progressive demineralization and renal injury.

references.label: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research 2022 Guidelines for the Management of Asymptomatic Primary Hyperparathyroidism

subject: Surgery
topic: Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm & Immediate Surgical Exploration
shortestValidSolution: Severe flank pain + pulsatile mass + shock (BP 78/46) + ultrasound showing 6.8 cm AAA rupture -> immediate operating room transfer.
necessaryInference: Recognize that hemodynamic instability in ruptured AAA mandates immediate surgical intervention without delaying for CT angiography.
strongestDistractor: Immediate CTA of the abdomen/pelvis, which is appropriate for stable patients but fatal in unstable patients.
distractorExclusion: Sending an unstable patient with ruptured AAA to the CT suite causes catastrophic delay and arrest outside the OR.

references.label: Journal of Vascular Surgery 2020 Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Practice Guidelines on the Care of Patients with an Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Acute Epiglottitis & Controlled Airway Management in Operating Room
shortestValidSolution: Unimmunized child with fever + drooling + tripod position + stridor = epiglottitis -> keep calm, avoid oral exam, secure airway in OR.
necessaryInference: Recognize the clinical emergency of epiglottitis and understand why direct exam or needle sticks trigger catastrophic airway collapse.
strongestDistractor: Direct examination of the posterior pharynx with a tongue blade, an intuitive reflex that triggers fatal laryngospasm.
distractorExclusion: Tongue depressor exam in suspected epiglottitis triggers acute complete airway obstruction and is strictly contraindicated outside an OR.

references.label: Pediatrics in Review 2021 Epiglottitis and Pediatric Stridor Emergencies

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Preterm Premature Rupture of Membranes (PPROM) Management at 31 Weeks
shortestValidSolution: PPROM at 31 weeks without chorioamnionitis -> latency antibiotics + betamethasone + magnesium sulfate (< 32w) + expectant management until 34 weeks.
necessaryInference: Select guideline-directed triple medical therapy (latency antibiotics, corticosteroids, magnesium) and expectant management to 34 weeks over premature delivery.
strongestDistractor: Immediate induction or cesarean delivery, which causes severe iatrogenic prematurity without clinical indication.
distractorExclusion: Delivery is deferred until 34 weeks in uncomplicated PPROM to allow fetal pulmonary maturation under antibiotic and corticosteroid coverage.

references.label: Obstetrics & Gynecology 2020 ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 217: Prelabor Rupture of Membranes

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Psychotic Depression: Combination Antidepressant-Antipsychotic Therapy
shortestValidSolution: Severe depression + somatic/persecutory delusions = psychotic depression -> antidepressant + second-generation antipsychotic (or ECT).
necessaryInference: Recognize psychotic depression and apply the evidence-based requirement for combination antidepressant-antipsychotic pharmacotherapy over monotherapy.
strongestDistractor: Antidepressant monotherapy, a common error based on treating unipolar depression while neglecting psychotic symptoms.
distractorExclusion: Antidepressant monotherapy fails in psychotic depression; both dopamine and serotonin/norepinephrine pathways must be targeted.

references.label: American Journal of Psychiatry 2020 Pharmacotherapy for Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Compartment Syndrome & Emergent Decompressive Fasciotomy
shortestValidSolution: Tibial fracture + pain with passive stretch + delta pressure <= 30 mmHg (76 - 52 = 24) -> emergent four-compartment fasciotomy.
necessaryInference: Identify compartment syndrome despite preserved distal pulses and recognize that a delta pressure <= 30 mmHg mandates immediate fasciotomy.
strongestDistractor: Elevating the leg above the heart, a common clinical mistake that decreases perfusion pressure and worsens compartment ischemia.
distractorExclusion: Limb elevation decreases local arteriovenous gradient and precipitates irreversible necrosis; emergent fasciotomy is mandatory.

references.label: Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery 2020 Acute Compartment Syndrome of the Lower Extremity

subject: Medicine
topic: Giant Cell Arteritis & Immediate Systemic Corticosteroids Before Biopsy
shortestValidSolution: New headache + jaw claudication + tender temporal artery + ESR 104 = GCA -> immediate high-dose corticosteroids before biopsy.
necessaryInference: Recognize the risk of immediate blindness in GCA and prioritize urgent corticosteroid initiation over awaiting biopsy confirmation.
strongestDistractor: Scheduling temporal artery biopsy before starting steroids to ensure histopathological diagnostic purity.
distractorExclusion: Awaiting biopsy before steroid therapy risks permanent ischemic blindness; histopathology remains accurate weeks after steroids start.

references.label: Arthritis & Rheumatology 2021 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Giant Cell Arteritis

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Moderate-to-Severe Croup: Nebulized Racemic Epinephrine & Dexamethasone
shortestValidSolution: Child with barking cough + inspiratory stridor at rest + steeple sign = moderate-severe croup -> nebulized racemic epinephrine + dexamethasone.
necessaryInference: Recognize stridor at rest as the threshold requiring nebulized racemic epinephrine alongside dexamethasone.
strongestDistractor: Nebulized albuterol, an asthma bronchodilator with no alpha-1 vasoconstrictive activity against subglottic edema.
distractorExclusion: Albuterol acts on lower airway beta-2 receptors and does not treat subglottic mucosal edema; alpha-1 adrenergic stimulation via epinephrine is required.

references.label: New England Journal of Medicine 2018 Acute Croup in Children

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Shoulder Dystocia: McRoberts Maneuver & Suprapubic Pressure Management
shortestValidSolution: Fetal head retracts against perineum (turtle sign) = shoulder dystocia -> stop pushing, McRoberts maneuver + suprapubic pressure.
necessaryInference: Select McRoberts maneuver and suprapubic pressure as the first-line interventions for shoulder dystocia and avoid dangerous fundal pressure.
strongestDistractor: Applying firm fundal pressure, a dangerous practice that impacts the fetal shoulder and risks uterine rupture.
distractorExclusion: Fundal pressure is strictly contraindicated in shoulder dystocia because it causes shoulder impaction, uterine rupture, and brachial plexus avulsion.

references.label: Obstetrics & Gynecology 2020 ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 178: Shoulder Dystocia

subject: Medicine
topic: Anaphylaxis Management: Intramuscular Epinephrine & Refractory Dosing Protocol
shortestValidSolution: Anaphylactic shock refractory 10 minutes after first IM epinephrine -> repeat IM epinephrine + rapid IV isotonic crystalloid boluses.
necessaryInference: Recognize that refractory anaphylaxis requires repeated IM epinephrine and IV fluid resuscitation rather than relying on slow secondary antihistamines or steroids.
strongestDistractor: Intravenous diphenhydramine and methylprednisolone, popular secondary agents that are completely ineffective at treating acute refractory shock.
distractorExclusion: Antihistamines and steroids do not treat distributive shock or laryngeal edema; repeat epinephrine is the sole life-saving intervention.

references.label: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology 2020 Anaphylaxis: A Practice Parameter Update

subject: Medicine
topic: Severe Hyperkalemia with ECG Changes: Intravenous Calcium Membrane Stabilization
shortestValidSolution: Potassium 7.6 mEq/L with peaked T waves and wide QRS -> immediate IV calcium gluconate to stabilize cardiac membrane.
necessaryInference: Sequence resuscitation properly: stabilize the cardiac membrane with IV calcium before attempting to shift or eliminate potassium.
strongestDistractor: Intravenous insulin and dextrose, which is necessary to lower potassium but takes 20 minutes and leaves the heart vulnerable to ventricular fibrillation without calcium.
distractorExclusion: Insulin takes 15–30 minutes to lower potassium; IV calcium acts in 1–3 minutes to prevent immediate lethal arrhythmias.

references.label: Circulation 2020 2020 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care: Hyperkalemia

subject: Medicine
topic: High-Risk Solitary Pulmonary Nodule: Tissue Biopsy vs Surveillance
shortestValidSolution: 1.8 cm spiculated upper-lobe nodule in 64yo smoker = high malignancy probability -> PET-CT or biopsy / surgical resection.
necessaryInference: Distinguish high-risk solitary nodules (> 8 mm, spiculated, smoker) requiring active tissue investigation from low-risk nodules managed with CT surveillance.
strongestDistractor: Repeat chest CT surveillance in 6–12 months, which is appropriate for low-risk nodules < 8 mm but dangerous for a 1.8-cm spiculated mass.
distractorExclusion: A 1.8-cm spiculated nodule has high malignancy risk (> 65%); delaying tissue diagnosis with 6-12 month surveillance allows tumor progression.

references.label: Radiology 2017 Guidelines for Management of Incidental Pulmonary Nodules Detected on CT Images: From the Fleischner Society 2017

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis: Preoperative Fluid & Electrolyte Resuscitation
shortestValidSolution: Pyloric stenosis + hypochloremic hypokalemic alkalosis -> IV fluid and potassium resuscitation first; defer pyloromyotomy until labs normalize.
necessaryInference: Recognize that pyloromyotomy is an elective procedure following medical stabilization, not an immediate surgical emergency.
strongestDistractor: Immediate transfer to the operating room for emergency pyloromyotomy, which causes fatal anesthetic apnea in alkalotic infants.
distractorExclusion: Operating prior to electrolyte normalization leads to hypoventilation, apnea, and arrhythmias under general anesthesia.

references.label: Pediatrics in Review 2020 Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis in Infants

subject: Neurology
topic: Guillain-Barré Syndrome: Serial Respiratory Parameter Monitoring & Immunotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Ascending paralysis + areflexia + CSF albuminocytologic dissociation = GBS -> serial bedside FVC/NIF monitoring + IVIG or plasma exchange.
necessaryInference: Recognize that respiratory failure in GBS is detected by ventilatory mechanics (FVC/NIF) rather than pulse oximetry, and select IVIG/plasmapheresis over steroids.
strongestDistractor: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, which works for multiple sclerosis flares but is proven ineffective in GBS.
distractorExclusion: Corticosteroids have no efficacy in GBS; IVIG and plasma exchange are the sole proven disease-modifying treatments.

references.label: Lancet Neurology 2021 Guillain-Barré Syndrome: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Fetal Growth Restriction & Umbilical Artery Doppler Absent End-Diastolic Flow
shortestValidSolution: FGR (< 10th percentile) at 32 weeks + absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) -> betamethasone + inpatient monitoring + delivery at 33–34 weeks.
necessaryInference: Recognize that AEDF mandates antenatal corticosteroids and scheduled delivery at 33–34 weeks rather than term expectant management.
strongestDistractor: Reassurance based on a normal reactive nonstress test and 4-week outpatient follow-up, which overlooks the high risk of sudden stillbirth.
distractorExclusion: A reactive NST does not prevent imminent placental failure; AEDF is an established indication for expedited delivery at 33–34 weeks.

references.label: American Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology 2020 SMFM Consult Series #52: Diagnosis and Management of Fetal Growth Restriction

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Delirium Diagnosis & Multicomponent Non-Pharmacological Management Strategy
shortestValidSolution: Acute fluctuating inattention in hospitalized elder with UTI = delirium -> non-pharmacological interventions + treat underlying infection.
necessaryInference: Identify delirium vs dementia and select evidence-based non-pharmacological interventions over chemical or physical restraints.
strongestDistractor: Immediate scheduled haloperidol, which is widely misused but carries FDA black box warnings and does not resolve delirium.
distractorExclusion: Antipsychotics do not treat or shorten delirium duration and increase mortality; non-pharmacological care is first-line.

references.label: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society 2020 American Geriatrics Society Clinical Practice Guideline for Postoperative Delirium

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Testicular Torsion: Emergent Surgical Exploration & Bilateral Orchiopexy
shortestValidSolution: Sudden severe scrotal pain + horizontal lie + absent cremasteric reflex = torsion -> immediate surgical exploration + bilateral orchiopexy.
necessaryInference: Recognize the 6-hour surgical urgency of testicular torsion and the mandatory requirement for bilateral orchiopexy.
strongestDistractor: Awaiting scrotal duplex Doppler ultrasound confirmation, which wastes precious ischemic time in a classic case within the 6-hour window.
distractorExclusion: Ultrasound delays operative management; classic torsion within the salvage window mandates immediate surgical exploration.

references.label: Journal of Pediatric Urology 2021 Testicular Torsion: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management

subject: Medicine
topic: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN: Drug Discontinuation & Burn ICU Care
shortestValidSolution: Lamotrigine + fever + mucosal ulcerations + 22% BSA epidermal detachment (positive Nikolsky) = SJS/TEN overlap -> stop drug + transfer to burn unit.
necessaryInference: Recognize SJS/TEN overlap and prioritize immediate drug cessation and burn unit transfer over antimicrobial therapy or surgical debridement.
strongestDistractor: Immediate aggressive surgical sharp debridement of all sloughing skin, which destroys viable dermis and worsens burn-like fluid loss.
distractorExclusion: SJS/TEN does not benefit from surgical debridement; the epidermis is managed with sterile non-adherent dressings in a burn unit.

references.label: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology 2020 Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis: Management Strategies

subject: Ethics
topic: Medical Error Disclosure & Transparent Physician Communication Protocol
shortestValidSolution: Wrong medication administered causing temporary arrest -> provide full transparent disclosure, apology, and outline systemic safety improvements.
necessaryInference: Recognize the ethical obligation of full disclosure and apology for medical errors regardless of whether permanent physical injury resulted.
strongestDistractor: Withholding disclosure because the patient suffered no permanent physical harm, an unethical stance that violates patient autonomy.
distractorExclusion: Transient harm that required emergency intubation is a major clinical event requiring mandatory transparent disclosure under AMA guidelines.

references.label: AMA Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 8.1: Routine Disclosure of Medical Errors

subject: Medicine
topic: Stanford Type A versus Type B Aortic Dissection Management
shortestValidSolution: Distinguish Stanford Type A (involves ascending aorta, requires emergent open surgical repair due to tamponade/coronary/aortic valve risk) from uncomplicated Type B (descending aorta distal to left subclavian, managed medically with IV beta-blockers targeting SBP 100-120 and HR < 60).
necessaryInference: Distinguish Stanford Type A (involves ascending aorta, requires emergent open surgical repair due to tamponade/coronary/aortic valve risk) from uncomplicated Type B (descending aorta distal to left subclavian, managed medically with IV beta-blockers targeting SBP 100-120 and HR < 60).
strongestDistractor: Emergent open surgical graft replacement with hypothermic circulatory arrest
distractorExclusion: Emergent open surgical repair is the mandatory immediate treatment for Stanford Type A aortic dissection (involving the ascending aorta) due to the high risk of fatal pericardial tamponade, aortic regurgitation, and coronary malperfusion; uncomplicated Type B dissection is managed medically.

references.label: Isselbacher EM, et al. 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease. Circulation. 2022;146(24):e334-e482. PMID: 36322642.

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Postpartum Hemorrhage Stepwise Uterotonic Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony (boggy uterus). Oxytocin and bimanual massage are first-line. Second-line uterotonics require knowing patient contraindications: Methylergonovine is contraindicated in hypertension; Carboprost tromethamine (PGF2alpha) is contraindicated in asthma. In a patient with chronic hypertension or preeclampsia, carboprost (or misoprostol/TXA) is selected over methylergonovine.
necessaryInference: Recognize postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony (boggy uterus). Oxytocin and bimanual massage are first-line. Second-line uterotonics require knowing patient contraindications: Methylergonovine is contraindicated in hypertension; Carboprost tromethamine (PGF2alpha) is contraindicated in asthma. In a patient with chronic hypertension or preeclampsia, carboprost (or misoprostol/TXA) is selected over methylergonovine.
strongestDistractor: Intramuscular methylergonovine maleate
distractorExclusion: Methylergonovine maleate is an ergot derivative that produces potent generalized arterial vasoconstriction and is contraindicated in patients with gestational hypertension, chronic hypertension, or preeclampsia due to the risk of catastrophic intracranial hemorrhage and malignant hypertension.

references.label: Committee on Practice Bulletins-Obstetrics. Practice Bulletin No. 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage. Obstet Gynecol. 2017;130(4):e168-e186. PMID: 28937571.

subject: Surgery
topic: Suspected Scaphoid Fracture with Negative Initial Radiographs
shortestValidSolution: Recognize fall on outstretched hand (FOOSH) with tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox. Initial plain radiographs can be falsely negative in up to 15-20% of nondisplaced scaphoid fractures. Management requires thumb spica splinting and repeat radiographs in 10-14 days (or immediate MRI) to prevent nonunion and avascular necrosis.
necessaryInference: Recognize fall on outstretched hand (FOOSH) with tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox. Initial plain radiographs can be falsely negative in up to 15-20% of nondisplaced scaphoid fractures. Management requires thumb spica splinting and repeat radiographs in 10-14 days (or immediate MRI) to prevent nonunion and avascular necrosis.
strongestDistractor: Application of an elastic compression bandage with immediate return to sports as tolerated
distractorExclusion: Treating this as a simple sprain without immobilization places the patient at high risk for nonunion and permanent wrist disability secondary to scaphoid avascular necrosis.

references.label: Duckworth AD, et al. Assessment and management of suspected scaphoid fractures. BMJ. 2012;344:e264. PMID: 22359495.

subject: Medicine
topic: Thyroid Storm Stepwise Pharmacotherapy and Wolff-Chaikoff Effect
shortestValidSolution: Recognize thyroid storm (fever, delirium, tachycardia/afib, heart failure, jaundice). Sequence of medications: 1. Beta-blocker (propranolol); 2. Thionamide (PTU preferred over methimazole as it blocks peripheral T4->T3 conversion); 3. Potassium iodide (Lugol solution or SSKI) must be administered >=1 HOUR AFTER thionamide to prevent using the iodine as new hormone substrate (Jod-Basedow effect); 4. Glucocorticoids (hydrocortisone).
necessaryInference: Recognize thyroid storm (fever, delirium, tachycardia/afib, heart failure, jaundice). Sequence of medications: 1. Beta-blocker (propranolol); 2. Thionamide (PTU preferred over methimazole as it blocks peripheral T4->T3 conversion); 3. Potassium iodide (Lugol solution or SSKI) must be administered >=1 HOUR AFTER thionamide to prevent using the iodine as new hormone substrate (Jod-Basedow effect); 4. Glucocorticoids (hydrocortisone).
strongestDistractor: Administer immediately before propylthiouracil to sensitize follicular cell iodine transporters
distractorExclusion: Administering iodine before a thionamide exacerbates thyrotoxicosis by fueling hormone synthesis, potentially inducing lethal arrhythmia or circulatory collapse.

references.label: Ross DS, et al. 2016 American Thyroid Association Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis. Thyroid. 2016;26(10):1343-1421. PMID: 27521067.

subject: Medicine
topic: Neutropenic Fever Post-Chemotherapy Emergent Monotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize neutropenic fever: single oral temp >= 38.3 C (101 F) with absolute neutrophil count (ANC) < 500/microL. Immediate empiric monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam, or meropenem) within 60 minutes. Vancomycin is NOT routinely indicated upfront unless specific criteria are met (hemodynamic instability, pneumonia, catheter site infection, severe mucositis).
necessaryInference: Recognize neutropenic fever: single oral temp >= 38.3 C (101 F) with absolute neutrophil count (ANC) < 500/microL. Immediate empiric monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam, or meropenem) within 60 minutes. Vancomycin is NOT routinely indicated upfront unless specific criteria are met (hemodynamic instability, pneumonia, catheter site infection, severe mucositis).
strongestDistractor: Combination therapy with intravenous vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin
distractorExclusion: Oral fluoroquinolones are used only for low-risk outpatient neutropenia (MASCC score >= 21) in combination with amoxicillin-clavulanate, not for inpatient neutropenic fever; vancomycin monotherapy lacks gram-negative coverage.

references.label: Freifeld AG, et al. Clinical practice guideline for the use of antimicrobial agents in neutropenic patients with cancer: 2010 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America. Clin Infect Dis. 2011;52(4):e56-e93. PMID: 21258094.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Ileocolic Intussusception Ultrasound Diagnosis and Air Enema Reduction
shortestValidSolution: Recognize episodic colicky abdominal pain (knees to chest), vomiting, lethargy, and currant jelly stool in a 6-24 month infant. Abdominal ultrasound is diagnostic method of choice (target / donut sign). Treatment is air or hydrostatic (contrast) enema reduction, provided there are no signs of peritonitis or bowel perforation.
necessaryInference: Recognize episodic colicky abdominal pain (knees to chest), vomiting, lethargy, and currant jelly stool in a 6-24 month infant. Abdominal ultrasound is diagnostic method of choice (target / donut sign). Treatment is air or hydrostatic (contrast) enema reduction, provided there are no signs of peritonitis or bowel perforation.
strongestDistractor: Emergent exploratory laparotomy with primary surgical resection of the cecum
distractorExclusion: Surgical exploration is indicated only when enema reduction fails, if the patient presents with signs of peritonitis, bowel perforation, shock, or when a pathological lead point is identified.

references.label: Kelley-Quon IQ, et al. Management of intussusception in children: a systematic review. J Pediatr Surg. 2021;56(3):587-596. PMID: 33189332.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma Immediate Medical Management Sequence
shortestValidSolution: Recognize acute angle-closure glaucoma (unilateral severe ocular pain, headache, halos around lights, fixed mid-dilated pupil, cloudy cornea, rock-hard globe, IOP > 40-50 mm Hg). Immediate medical therapy combines topical pressure-lowering agents (timolol, apraclonidine, pilocarpine) and systemic agents (IV acetazolamide or IV mannitol). Definitive treatment is laser peripheral iridotomy.
necessaryInference: Recognize acute angle-closure glaucoma (unilateral severe ocular pain, headache, halos around lights, fixed mid-dilated pupil, cloudy cornea, rock-hard globe, IOP > 40-50 mm Hg). Immediate medical therapy combines topical pressure-lowering agents (timolol, apraclonidine, pilocarpine) and systemic agents (IV acetazolamide or IV mannitol). Definitive treatment is laser peripheral iridotomy.
strongestDistractor: Topical cyclopentolate, topical phenylephrine, and oral prednisone
distractorExclusion: Cyclopentolate and phenylephrine are mydriatic agents that cause pupil dilation, which would further bunch the peripheral iris into the iridocorneal angle and worsen angle-closure.

references.label: Weinreb RN, et al. Primary open-angle glaucoma. Lancet. 2014;383(9930):1739-1748. PMID: 24529763.

subject: Obstetrics
topic: Ectopic Pregnancy Methotrexate Candidacy versus Laparoscopy
shortestValidSolution: Evaluate methotrexate candidacy for unruptured ectopic pregnancy: Hemodynamically stable, beta-hCG < 5,000 mIU/mL, ectopic gestational sac < 3.5-4 cm, no fetal cardiac activity, patient willing to comply with follow-up, and normal hepatic/renal function. Laparoscopy is indicated if hemodynamically unstable, peritoneal signs, contraindications to methotrexate, mass > 3.5 cm, cardiac activity present, or beta-hCG > 5,000.
necessaryInference: Evaluate methotrexate candidacy for unruptured ectopic pregnancy: Hemodynamically stable, beta-hCG < 5,000 mIU/mL, ectopic gestational sac < 3.5-4 cm, no fetal cardiac activity, patient willing to comply with follow-up, and normal hepatic/renal function. Laparoscopy is indicated if hemodynamically unstable, peritoneal signs, contraindications to methotrexate, mass > 3.5 cm, cardiac activity present, or beta-hCG > 5,000.
strongestDistractor: Immediate diagnostic and therapeutic laparoscopy with right salpingectomy
distractorExclusion: Surgical laparoscopy (salpingectomy or salpingostomy) is indicated for hemodynamic instability, symptoms of tubal rupture (peritoneal signs), contraindications to methotrexate, ectopic mass >= 3.5 cm, or beta-hCG > 5,000 mIU/mL.

references.label: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists' Committee on Practice Bulletins—Gynecology. ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 193: Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy. Obstet Gynecol. 2018;131(3):e91-e103. PMID: 29470343.

subject: Surgery
topic: Obstructing Urolithiasis with Urosepsis Emergent Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Recognize infected obstructed kidney (ureteral stone + fever, leukocytosis, pyuria, hydronephrosis). This is a surgical urological emergency. Immediate decompression via percutaneous nephrostomy tube or retrograde ureteral stent placement under IV broad-spectrum antibiotics. Shock-wave lithotripsy and ureteroscopy are strictly contraindicated during acute infection.
necessaryInference: Recognize infected obstructed kidney (ureteral stone + fever, leukocytosis, pyuria, hydronephrosis). This is a surgical urological emergency. Immediate decompression via percutaneous nephrostomy tube or retrograde ureteral stent placement under IV broad-spectrum antibiotics. Shock-wave lithotripsy and ureteroscopy are strictly contraindicated during acute infection.
strongestDistractor: Emergent extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy to fragment the obstructing ureteral calculus
distractorExclusion: Shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) is absolutely contraindicated in the presence of active urinary tract infection because stone fragmentation disperses infected debris and bacteria into the circulation, precipitating septic shock.

references.label: Assimos D, et al. Surgical Management of Stones: American Urological Association/Endourological Society Guideline. J Urol. 2016;196(4):1153-1160. PMID: 27238616.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Screening and Ultrasound
shortestValidSolution: Recognize risk factors for DDH (breech presentation, female, family history) or positive Ortolani/Barlow sign. In infants < 4-6 months of age, the femoral head is predominantly cartilaginous; therefore, ultrasound of the hips is the diagnostic imaging modality of choice. Plain radiographs are only reliable after 4-6 months when the femoral head ossifies.
necessaryInference: Recognize risk factors for DDH (breech presentation, female, family history) or positive Ortolani/Barlow sign. In infants < 4-6 months of age, the femoral head is predominantly cartilaginous; therefore, ultrasound of the hips is the diagnostic imaging modality of choice. Plain radiographs are only reliable after 4-6 months when the femoral head ossifies.
strongestDistractor: Anteroposterior and frog-leg lateral radiographs of the pelvis
distractorExclusion: Plain radiography of the pelvis is the imaging modality of choice only after 4 to 6 months of age, once the femoral head ossification center has developed sufficiently to allow measurement of the acetabular index.

references.label: Shaw BA, et al. Evaluation and referral for developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants. Pediatrics. 2016;138(6):e20163107. PMID: 27940748.

subject: Surgery
topic: Tension Pneumothorax Immediate Needle Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate tension pneumothorax from cardiac tamponade in trauma. Both cause hypotension and JVD. Tension pneumothorax features absent unilateral breath sounds, hyperresonance to percussion, and contralateral tracheal deviation. Immediate treatment is needle decompression (2nd intercostal space midclavicular or 5th intercostal anterior axillary line) followed by tube thoracostomy, without waiting for a chest radiograph.
necessaryInference: Differentiate tension pneumothorax from cardiac tamponade in trauma. Both cause hypotension and JVD. Tension pneumothorax features absent unilateral breath sounds, hyperresonance to percussion, and contralateral tracheal deviation. Immediate treatment is needle decompression (2nd intercostal space midclavicular or 5th intercostal anterior axillary line) followed by tube thoracostomy, without waiting for a chest radiograph.
strongestDistractor: Hold interventions until portable anteroposterior chest radiography confirms the pleural line
distractorExclusion: Tension pneumothorax is a strictly clinical diagnosis; delaying decompression to obtain radiographs frequently leads to pulseless electrical activity (PEA) arrest and death.

references.label: American College of Surgeons. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago, IL: American College of Surgeons; 2018.

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Catatonia Lorazepam Challenge and Electroconvulsive Therapy
shortestValidSolution: Recognize catatonia (immobility, mutism, stupor, waxy flexibility, posturing, negativism) associated with severe mood disorders or psychotic disorders. First-line diagnostic and therapeutic intervention is the intravenous lorazepam challenge test (1-2 mg IV), which provides rapid temporary relief. Definitive therapy for refractory catatonia or malignant catatonia is electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). Antipsychotics are contraindicated as they can worsen catatonia or precipitate NMS.

First-line diagnostic and therapeutic intervention is the intravenous lorazepam challenge test (1-2 mg IV), which provides rapid temporary relief. Definitive therapy for refractory catatonia or malignant catatonia is electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). Antipsychotics are contraindicated as they can worsen catatonia or precipitate NMS.
strongestDistractor: Intramuscular haloperidol administration targeting underlying psychotic thought disorder
distractorExclusion: First-generation and second-generation antipsychotics are strictly contraindicated in acute catatonia because dopamine D2 receptor antagonism exacerbates catatonia and dramatically increases the risk of precipitating neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS).

references.label: Sienaert P, et al. Evidence-based treatment for catatonia: a systematic review. Curr Psychiatry Rep. 2014;16(7):450. PMID: 24838688.

subject: Medicine
topic: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Diagnostic Paracentesis and Albumin
shortestValidSolution: Recognize spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (cirrhosis with ascites + fever, abdominal pain, or altered mental status). Diagnostic paracentesis shows ascitic fluid absolute neutrophil count (PMN) >= 250/microL. Immediate empiric coverage is IV third-generation cephalosporin (cefotaxime or ceftriaxone) PLUS intravenous albumin (1.5 g/kg on day 1, 1.0 g/kg on day 3) to prevent hepatorenal syndrome and reduce mortality.
necessaryInference: Recognize spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (cirrhosis with ascites + fever, abdominal pain, or altered mental status). Diagnostic paracentesis shows ascitic fluid absolute neutrophil count (PMN) >= 250/microL. Immediate empiric coverage is IV third-generation cephalosporin (cefotaxime or ceftriaxone) PLUS intravenous albumin (1.5 g/kg on day 1, 1.0 g/kg on day 3) to prevent hepatorenal syndrome and reduce mortality.
strongestDistractor: Immediate placement of a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS)
distractorExclusion: TIPS is contraindicated during active systemic infection or peritonitis; it is used for refractory ascites or secondary prevention of variceal bleeding once infection is eradicated.

references.label: Biggins SW, et al. Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management of Ascites and Complications in Cirrhosis: 2021 Practice Guidance by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases. Hepatology. 2021;74(2):1014-1048. PMID: 33942342.

subject: Medicine
topic: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Primary Prevention of Sudden Death
shortestValidSolution: Identify hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). topic: Kawasaki Disease Intravenous Immunoglobulin and Coronary Aneurysms

topic: Acute Limb Ischemia Six Ps and Immediate Anticoagulation

topic: Carbon Monoxide Toxicity Co-Oximetry and Hyperbaric Oxygen

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Ventricular Septal Defect Eisenmenger Syndrome Prevention

subject: Medicine
topic: Exertional Heat Stroke Immediate Cold Water Immersion

subject: Medicine
topic: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State Fluid Resuscitation and Potassium
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS): elderly type 2 diabetic, severe hyperglycemia (> 600-1,000 mg/dL), high effective serum osmolality (> 320 mOsm/kg), minimal/absent ketones, and profound dehydration (fluid deficit 8-10 liters) with altered mental status. subject: Surgery
topic: Perforated Peptic Ulcer Pneumoperitoneum Surgical Emergency

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia Superior Mesenteric Artery Embolism

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Pancreatitis Fluid Resuscitation and Gallstone Workup

GOAL-DIRECTED INTRAVENOUS FLUID RESUSCITATION: LACTATED RINGER'S solution (200-500 mL/hr, or 20 mL/kg bolus followed by 3 mL/kg/hr) is SUPERIOR to normal saline (reduces systemic inflammation and SIRS); 2. INDICATIONS FOR ERCP: ERCP within 24 hours is indicated ONLY for acute gallstone pancreatitis with CONCURRENT ACUTE CHOLANGITIS or persistent common bile duct obstruction. subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Cholangitis Reynolds Pentad Emergent Biliary Decompression

DEFINITIVE EMERGENCY THERAPY: EMERGENT BILIARY DECOMPRESSION VIA ERCP (endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with sphincterotomy, stone extraction, and stent placement) within 12 to 24 hours. subject: Surgery
topic: Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Hemodynamic Instability Management

IN A HEMODYNAMICALLY UNSTABLE PATIENT WITH A KNOWN AAA (or classic triad): IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY TRANSFER TO THE OPERATING ROOM FOR LAPAROTOMY OR ENDOVASCULAR ANEURYSM REPAIR (EVAR). subject: Medicine
topic: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy Indications
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning and Hyperbaric Oxygen (HBO) indications: CO binds hemoglobin with 250x affinity of O2 (carboxyhemoglobin, COHb) and alters allosteric structure, shifting curve leftward (impairing offloading) and inhibiting mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase. Symptoms: headache, nausea, confusion, cherry-red skin, coma, myocardial ischemia. INITIAL MANAGEMENT: 100% NORMOBARIC OXYGEN via non-rebreather mask (reduces COHb half-life from 300 minutes to 90 minutes). INDICATIONS FOR IMMEDIATE HYPERBARIC OXYGEN (HBO, 2.5-3.0 atm; reduces half-life to 30 minutes, displaces CO from tissues and prevents delayed neuropsychiatric sequelae): 1. CARBOXYHEMOGLOBIN > 25% (or > 15% in PREGNANCY, because fetal hemoglobin binds CO avidly); 2. LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS, syncope, or coma; 3. SEVERE METABOLIC ACIDOSIS (pH < 7.1-7.25); 4. EVIDENCE OF END-ORGAN ISCHEMIA (myocardial ischemia/infarction, ECG changes, acute neurological deficits).

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma Immediate Medical Management Sequence
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma (AACG): ophthalmic emergency. Sudden blockage of aqueous humor outflow through the trabecular meshwork at the iridocorneal angle. Triggers: entering a dark room (pupillary dilation folds iris into angle), anticholinergics, sympathomimetics. Symptoms: sudden, severe unilateral eye pain, headache, nausea/vomiting, seeing HALOS AROUND LIGHTS. Physical exam: FIXED, MID-DILATED PUPIL, steamy hazy cornea, conjunctival ciliary injection, and a "ROCK-HARD" globe on palpation. Tonometry confirms markedly elevated INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE (IOP > 30-50 mm Hg; normal 10-21). IMMEDIATE MEDICAL THERAPY TO LOWER IOP: Combination of: 1. Topical beta-blocker (TIMOLOL); 2. Topical alpha-2 agonist (APRACLONIDINE); 3. Topical muscarinic miotic (PILOCARPINE, constricts pupil to pull iris away from angle; given once IOP < 40); 4. Systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (oral/IV ACETAZOLAMIDE) or IV MANNITOL. DEFINITIVE TREATMENT: LASER PERIPHERAL IRIDOTOMY in BOTH eyes. CONTRAINDICATION: Mydriatics (atropine, phenylephrine) are strictly prohibited!

subject: Surgery
topic: Cauda Equina Syndrome vs Conus Medullaris Surgical Decompression
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Cauda Equina Syndrome (CES) from Conus Medullaris Syndrome: 1. CAUDA EQUINA SYNDROME: compression of lumbosacral nerve roots (L2-S5) BELOW the conus medullaris (below L1-L2 vertebra, e.g., massive central L4-L5 disc herniation, tumor, trauma). Pure LOWER MOTOR NEURON (LMN) lesion: ASYMMETRIC, severe radicular shooting leg pain; asymmetric flaccid leg weakness; HYPOREFLEXIA/AREFLEXIA (absent ankle and knee jerks); SADDLE ANESTHESIA (loss of sensation in S3-S5 dermatomes: perineum, perianal, buttocks, inner thighs); and LATE autonomic dysfunction (urinary retention with overflow incontinence [post-void residual > 200 mL], decreased anal sphincter tone). 2. CONUS MEDULLARIS SYNDROME: injury to distal spinal cord at L1-L2; mixed UMN/LMN, symmetric pain, early fecal/urinary incontinence, bilateral hyperreflexia or Babinski. MANAGEMENT OF CAUDA EQUINA: 1. IMMEDIATE EMERGENT LUMBAR SPINE MRI; 2. EMERGENT SURGICAL DECOMPRESSION (laminectomy/discectomy) WITHIN 24-48 HOURS to prevent permanent paralysis and irreversible bowel/bladder incontinence.

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Gouty Arthritis Flare Medical Management Contraindications

Rapid changes in serum urate destabilize microtophi and prolong/worsen the acute flare.

subject: Medicine
topic: Severe Hyperkalemia with Electrocardiographic Changes Treatment Sequence

subject: Medicine
topic: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis Albumin Infusion and Antibiotic Selection
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis (SBP): primary infection of ascitic fluid in patients with cirrhosis and portal hypertension. subject: Medicine
topic: Post-Cardiac Arrest Targeted Temperature Management Protocol

Target a CONSTANT CORE TEMPERATURE BETWEEN 32 C AND 36 C (or strictly maintain < 37.5 C to prevent fever) for at least 24 HOURS, using surface cooling blankets or intravascular catheters. Emergent Coronary Angiography (cath lab) if STEMI is present on post-ROSC ECG; 3. subject: Medicine
topic: Acetaminophen Toxicity Nomogram Timing and N-Acetylcysteine
shortestValidSolution: Manage Toxic Acetaminophen (Paracetamol) Ingestion: Most common cause of acute liver failure in the United States. Pathogenesis: At therapeutic doses, 90% is glucuronidated/sulfated; 5-10% is metabolized by CYP2E1 into N-ACETYL-P-BENZOQUINONE IMINE (NAPQI), a highly toxic reactive intermediate immediately detoxified by hepatic GLUTATHIONE. In overdose, sulfation/glucuronidation pathways are saturated, CYP2E1 shunts massive drug into NAPQI, depleting glutathione. NAC acts as a glutathione precursor and substitute, completely preventing hepatotoxicity if given within 8 hours. If ingestion time is unknown or presentation is late (> 24 hours) with elevated transaminases, give NAC immediately without waiting for nomograms.

topic: Ectopic Pregnancy Medical vs Surgical Management Contraindications

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis Resuscitation Priorities

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Intussusception Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approach

subject: Medicine

subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Salicylate Toxicity Pathophysiology and Management

subject: Medicine
topic: Tricyclic Antidepressant Overdose Electrocardiogram Abnormalities
shortestValidSolution: Recognize TCA Overdose (amitriptyline, nortriptyline): 1. Anticholinergic toxidrome (hyperthermia, mydriasis, flushed dry skin, delirium, urinary retention); 2. ECG FINDINGS: QRS PROLONGATION (> 100 ms predicts seizures, > 160 ms predicts ventricular arrhythmias), right axis deviation, terminal R wave > 3 mm in aVR. topic: Acute Iron Poisoning Clinical Phases and Chelation

GI stage (0-6 hours: abdominal pain, hematemesis, melena); 2. Latent quiescent stage (6-24 hours); 3. Shock/Metabolic acidosis stage (12-48 hours: severe lactic acidosis, hepatic necrosis, coagulopathy); 4. Hepatic failure (2-3 days); 5. Bowel obstruction (2-6 weeks: gastric outlet/pyloric scarring). - DIAGNOSIS: Radiopaque pills on abdominal X-ray, high serum iron (> 350-500 mcg/dL). - TREATMENT: INTRAVENOUS DEFEROXAMINE (chelates ferric iron to form ferrioxamine, excreted in urine turning it "vin rosé" reddish-pink).

subject: Medicine
topic: Digoxin Toxicity Manifestations and Digoxin-Specific Fab Fragments

AVOID CALCIUM (traditionally avoided due to risk of "stone heart" tetanic contracture).

subject: Medicine
topic: Lead Poisoning Clinical Recognition and Chelation Indications
shortestValidSolution: Manage Lead Poisoning (plumbism): Exposure in workers (battery, foundry, demolition) or children (lead paint in pre-1978 homes). subject: Pediatrics
topic: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia Evaluation and Phototherapy Thresholds
shortestValidSolution: Differentiate Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia: 1. UNCONJUGATED (INDIRECT) HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA: Risk of BIND (bilirubin-induced neurologic dysfunction) / KERNICTERUS (basal ganglia/brainstem deposition). Jaundice within FIRST 24 HOURS is ALWAYS PATHOLOGIC (most commonly ABO or Rh hemolytic disease). Manage based on nomograms: INTENSIVE PHOTOTHERAPY; if total serum bilirubin (TSB) approaches/exceeds exchange threshold (e.g. >= 20-25 mg/dL depending on hours of life and neurotoxicity risk factors) or signs of encephalopathy: IMMEDIATE EXCHANGE TRANSFUSION. 2. CONJUGATED (DIRECT > 20% of TSB): Biliary atresia (pale stools, dark urine; requires Kasai procedure).

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Acute Epiglottitis Airway Prioritization and Antimicrobial Coverage

X-ray shows "thumbprint sign" (do NOT obtain if patient in distress). CRITICAL AIRWAY RULE: MINIMIZE AGITATION. IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT: TRANSPORT DIRECTLY TO OPERATING ROOM WITH ANESTHESIOLOGY AND ENT FOR CONTROLLED ENDOTRACHEAL INTUBATION under inhalational anesthesia, followed by IV ceftriaxone + vancomycin.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Pediatric Ingestion of Button Batteries vs Blunt Foreign Bodies

TREATMENT: IMMEDIATE EMERGENT ENDOSCOPIC REMOVAL (or early honey/sucralfate ingestion to coat battery prior to endoscopy if child > 1 year). subject: Pediatrics
topic: Acute Bacterial Meningitis in Children Empiric Regimen and Adjuncts

subject: Medicine
topic: Post-Cardiac Arrest Targeted Temperature Management
shortestValidSolution: Manage Post-Cardiac Arrest Care after Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC): In comatose patients (not following commands): 1. TARGETED TEMPERATURE MANAGEMENT (TTM): Maintain a constant core body temperature between 32°C and 36°C (or strict fever prevention < 37.5°C) for at least 24 hours. Mechanism: Lowers cerebral metabolic demand, suppresses free radical generation, and inhibits ischemic neuronal apoptosis, significantly improving neurological recovery. 2. subject: Medicine
topic: Acute Ischemic Stroke Thrombolysis Eligibility and Blood Pressure Goals
shortestValidSolution: Manage Acute Ischemic Stroke: Window for IV Alteplase (or Tenecteplase) is < 4.5 hours from last known normal. subject: Medicine
topic: Status Epilepticus First- and Second-Line Pharmacotherapy
shortestValidSolution: Manage Convulsive Status Epilepticus (continuous seizure >= 5 minutes or >= 2 seizures without full recovery of consciousness between): - FIRST-LINE EMERGENCE (0-10 min): INTRAVENOUS LORAZEPAM (or IM Midazolam if no IV access). - SECOND-LINE URGENT CONTROL (10-30 min): NON-SEDATING ANTISEIZURE MEDICATION (IV LEVETIRACETAM, FOSPHENYTOIN, or SODIUM VALPROATE). - REFRACTORY STATUS (> 30 min): Continuous general anesthetic infusion (PROPOFOL, MIDAZOLAM, or PENTOBARBITAL) with endotracheal intubation and continuous EEG monitoring.

subject: Medicine
topic: Myasthenic Crisis Respiratory Failure and Management

subject: Medicine
topic: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Medical and Surgical Priorities
shortestValidSolution: Manage Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH, ruptured saccular/berry aneurysm): Diagnosis: Non-contrast head CT (high sensitivity in first 6 hours); if negative and clinical suspicion high: LUMBAR PUNCTURE (shows xanthochromia and persistently elevated RBCs from tube 1 to tube 4). subject: Medicine
topic: Giant Cell (Temporal) Arteritis Immediate Glucocorticoid Therapy

subject: Medicine
topic: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus Diagnosis and Treatment

Cognitive impairment / dementia. - NEUROIMAGING: Ventriculomegaly out of proportion to cerebral sulcal atrophy (Evans index > 0.3). - CONFIRMATORY DIAGNOSTIC TEST: HIGH-VOLUME LUMBAR PUNCTURE (tap test: removal of 30-50 mL CSF) demonstrating OBJECTIVE IMPROVEMENT IN GAIT SPEED AND STRIDE LENGTH. - DEFINITIVE TREATMENT: VENTRICULOPERITONEAL (VP) SHUNT.

subject: Medicine
topic: Wernicke Encephalopathy Recognition and Sequence of Vitamin Repletion

ENCEPHALOPATHY (confusion, disorientation, apathy); 2. OCULOMOTOR DYSFUNCTION (horizontal nystagmus, bilateral abducens [CN VI] palsy, conjugate gaze palsy); 3. GOLDEN RULE: ADMINISTER HIGH-DOSE INTRAVENOUS THIAMINE BEFORE OR CONCURRENTLY WITH INTRAVENOUS DEXTROSE.

topic: Tumor Lysis Syndrome Prevention and Rasburicase Mechanism

topic: Malignant Epidural Spinal Cord Compression Emergency Protocol

subject: Medicine
topic: Severe Hypercalcemia of Malignancy Management Hierarchy

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Clozapine-Induced Agranulocytosis Monitoring and Management

SEVERE NEUTROPENIA / AGRANULOCYTOSIS (ANC < 1000, and specifically < 500/mm³): IMMEDIATELY AND PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE CLOZAPINE. Admit, obtain infectious workup, and NEVER rechallenge.

subject: Psychiatry
topic: Acute Catatonia Diagnosis and Lorazepam Challenge

subject: Geriatrics
topic: Delirium vs Dementia Differentiation and Non-Pharmacologic Management

subject: Surgery
topic: Acute Compartment Syndrome Recognition and Fasciotomy

subject: Surgery
topic: Scaphoid Fracture Management with Negative Initial Radiographs

topic: Open Fracture Initial Emergency Management Sequence

subject: Surgery
topic: Posterior Hip Dislocation Presentation and Emergency Reduction

subject: Surgery
topic: Necrotizing Fasciitis Diagnostic Urgency and Surgical Debridement

NEVER DELAY SURGERY FOR IMAGING.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Septic Arthritis vs Transient Synovitis Kocher Criteria

topic: Prosthetic Joint Infection Classification and Two-Stage Revision

subject: Medicine
topic: Fat Embolism Syndrome Pathophysiology and Clinical Triad

topic: Lung Cancer Screening Criteria (USPSTF)

Currently smoke OR have quit within the past 15 years. - DISCONTINUATION CRITERIA: Stop screening once the person reaches age 81, has not smoked for > 15 years, or develops a severe health condition that substantially limits life expectancy or ability to undergo curative lung surgery. topic: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Screening Guidelines (USPSTF)

topic: Cervical Cancer Screening and Discontinuation Age Rules

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Tetralogy of Fallot Hypercyanotic "Tet Spell" Management
shortestValidSolution: Manage Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF: VSD, Overriding Aorta, Pulmonary Infundibular Stenosis, RV Hypertrophy): - HYPERCYANOTIC "TET SPELL": Triggered by crying, feeding, or exertion, which causes infundibular spasm or drops systemic vascular resistance (SVR). Right-to-left shunt across the VSD increases, sending deoxygenated blood to systemic organs -> profound cyanosis, tachypnea, syncope. - FIRST-LINE LIFESAVING INTERVENTION: KNEE-CHEST POSITION (or squatting in older children). MECHANISM: Flexing knees acutely kinks the femoral arteries, dramatically INCREASING SYSTEMIC VASCULAR RESISTANCE (SVR). Increased SVR reverses the shunt gradient across the VSD, forcing deoxygenated blood through the stenotic pulmonary outflow tract to the lungs for oxygenation. Secondary adjuncts: 100% O2, IV morphine, IV phenylephrine.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Coarctation of the Aorta Clinical Signs and Turner Syndrome Association
shortestValidSolution: Recognize Coarctation of the Aorta: Congenital narrowing of the aortic lumen, classically adjacent to the ductus arteriosus (juxtaductal). - ASSOCIATIONS: BICUSPID AORTIC VALVE (> 50-85% of cases) and TURNER SYNDROME (45,XO). - CLINICAL HALLMARK: UPPER EXTREMITY HYPERTENSION WITH LOWER EXTREMITY HYPOTENSION, accompanied by DIMINISHED OR DELAYED FEMORAL PULSES (RADIAL-FEMORAL PULSE LAG). - CHEST X-RAY: INFERIOR RIB NOTCHING (erosions on 3rd-8th ribs due to dilated collateral intercostal arteries) and "FIGURE-3 SIGN" on aorta. - CONFIRMATION: ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY or CT/MR angiography. Treatment: Balloon angioplasty / surgical resection.

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Transposition of the Great Arteries Immediate Prostaglandin E1

subject: Pediatrics
topic: Ventricular Septal Defect Natural History and Management
shortestValidSolution: Manage Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD, most common congenital heart defect): - SMALL RESTRICTIVE VSD (e.g., small muscular VSD): Loud, harsh, high-pitched HOLOSYSTOLIC MURMUR at LEFT LOWER STERNAL BORDER with palpable thrill; ASYMPTOMATIC, normal growth and development. shortestValidSolution: Manage Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Compression of the MEDIAN NERVE beneath the transverse carpal ligament (flexor retinaculum). - RISK FACTORS: Repetitive wrist flexion/extension, obesity, pregnancy, diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, hypothyroidism. - CLINICAL SIGNS: Paresthesias/pain in THUMB, INDEX, MIDDLE FINGER, and radial half of ring finger (sparing the thenar eminence because palmar cutaneous branch branches proximal to carpal tunnel). Symptoms worse at night. Positive Phalen test (flexion of wrists reproduces numbness) and Tinel sign. Thenar atrophy is a late finding. - FIRST-LINE INITIAL THERAPY: NOCTURNAL WRIST SPLINTING IN A NEUTRAL POSITION (relieves elevated intracarpal canal pressures during sleep). Second-line: Local corticosteroid injection; Refractory/severe: Surgical transverse carpal ligament release.

topic: GERD with Alarm Symptoms Diagnostic Approach
